This paper presents a new optimization-based receding horizon control method, termed proximal predictive control (PPC), designed to address constrained nonlinear systems. The core of the proposed approach involves solving an auxiliary optimization problem at every time step to update the control input. This auxiliary problem incorporates a regularization term that encourages a trajectory close to the solution of the preceding time step, thereby ensuring system robustness. A critical advantage of the PPC method is its ability to utilize general-purpose proximal algorithms for solving the optimization at each interval, which allows for the use of fewer control inputs compared to traditional model predictive control (MPC). Furthermore, the theoretical framework establishes the stability of trajectories for various system types, including globally stable linear systems and systems with locally stable nonlinear dynamics. Simulation results demonstrate that PPC effectively manages systems with stability requirements and performance objectives, while also providing superior robustness when subjected to disturbances and model uncertainties.

Stock market sentiment analysis has become increasingly vital for investors and financial institutions, as it can help predict market movements. This study examines the influence of online news sentiment and headlines on the S&P 500 index, utilizing a dataset comprising 100,000 data points from Yahoo Finance. The analysis employs a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model, which is well-suited for processing sequential information. By applying this model, the authors achieved a 0.06 percentage point increase in the S&P 500's prediction accuracy. Furthermore, sentiment analysis of news content was found to be a significant factor in enhancing overall forecasting precision.

The common envelope (CE) phase represents a critical juncture in binary evolution, during which an evolved star engulfs its companion, triggering complex interactions that drive orbital evolution. While extensive research has focused on the mechanisms of mass transfer and momentum exchange within the envelope, the fate of the engulfed primary star has received comparatively little attention. This study demonstrates that ionization fronts generated by the ionizing radiation of the companion can drive a wind from the ionized layer, leading to mass loss from the primary star. A two-dimensional radiation-hydrodynamical simulation of the interaction between a radiation front and stellar atmosphere confirms that if the front propagates sufficiently deep into the stellar envelope, this irradiation-induced phenomenon causes mass shedding. Furthermore, a one-dimensional, three-flux radiative-hydrodynamic model was employed to analyze how the front propagates through the stellar envelope. Our findings indicate that for a main-sequence companion emitting an ultraviolet flux corresponding to a 30 solar luminosity O-type star, the front can penetrate deep into the envelope of a red giant with an effective temperature of 3000 K and surface gravity of 10^3 cm s^-2 (specifically log g = 10^3 cgs units). This process results in mass-loss rates reaching 10^-3 solar masses per year, a magnitude comparable to that produced by common envelope ejection mechanisms.

We analyze double Higgs production via top-quark loops at the TeV scale within the Higgs Effective Field Theory (EFT), utilizing the background field method to derive the leading-order effective Lagrangian directly in terms of two Higgs fields. Our results demonstrate that, at energy scales significantly above the electroweak scale ($\sqrt{s} \gg v$), the longitudinal component of the production amplitude becomes dominant, scaling as $\mathcal{O}(s^2/v^4)$, whereas transverse contributions scale only as $\mathcal{O}(s^0/v^4)$. This behavior contrasts with single Higgs production, where such leading longitudinal terms are absent at this order. We further observe that leading-order effective couplings for two Higgs bosons exhibit a high degree of interdependence. Furthermore, we find that the impact of one-loop effective operators on double Higgs production is comparable to that of tree-level operators.

By applying the standard Leibniz rule to these derivatives, we obtain a result containing $O(1/c^2)$ terms that are inconsistent with general relativity. Consequently, we redefine the derivative operator to incorporate necessary corrections. Applying this corrected rule to the four-velocity and four-velocity tensor yields a four-velocity $U^\mu = (1, \vec v)$ and a four-momentum $P^\mu = (E, \vec p)$, which correctly reduce to their non-relativistic counterparts at leading order. However, when summed over a closed spatial loop, the four-velocity and four-momentum fail to vanish at subleading orders, violating fundamental geometric requirements. Furthermore, this modification introduces spurious $1/c^2$ contributions to the equations of motion, and the resulting four-velocity no longer satisfies the standard orthogonality condition with respect to the four-velocity vector.

This study examines the forces of drag acting on cylindrical intruders falling through two-dimensional granular assemblies at various packing densities. By analyzing the difference between the drag parallel to the cylinder's axis and the drag perpendicular to it, the research investigates how anisotropy varies with the geometry of the intruder. Specifically, the work explores the transition from anisotropic to isotropic drag regimes as the length-to-diameter ratio ($L/D$) increases. The findings indicate that the exponent characterizing this transition depends on whether the cylinders settle vertically or are inserted at an inclination. Furthermore, the study addresses the discrepancy between the observed behavior and previous three-dimensional simulations, which suggest a $1/D$ scaling for large $L/D$ ratios; the current results imply that dimensionality significantly influences the behavior of cylindrical objects within granular media.

The question of whether starbursting galaxies can generate outflows massive enough to halt star formation and trigger galaxy quenching remains a leading inquiry in astrophysics. We present new observations of the nearby starbursting galaxy NGC 3351, utilizing the Hubble Space Telescope's ACS/WFC2 to map the spatial distribution of ionized gas and the ALMA 1.3 mm continuum to identify dusty structures. By combining these datasets, we traced the trajectories of both dusty and non-dusty outflows, determining their kinematics and masses. Our findings reveal that the galaxy hosts two distinct outflows: a primary, massive dusty component moving away from the galactic disk along the line of sight, and a secondary, ionized gas stream emerging from the disk edges at roughly 45 degrees relative to the line of sight. We further calculated the mass flux of the latter outflow at $10^{-3} M_{\odot} yr^{-1} kpc^{-2}$, a value comparable to previous estimates for similar systems. This derived flux adheres to the established correlation between outflow mass flux and star formation rate surface density ($\Sigma_{SFR}$), expressed as $M_{out}/A \propto \Sigma_{SFR}^{1.5}$. Structured Bayesian Optimization (SBO) represents a strategy for global optimization that integrates knowledge from prior runs to narrow the search space, thereby accelerating convergence. Although BBO offers theoretical benefits, its practical application requires well-defined structures. In the context of computer system tuning, where the vast configuration space and prohibitive testing costs make exploring all possibilities unfeasible, this study investigates whether domain experts can effectively establish such structures. We introduce a new experimental framework designed to test the viability of structuring an optimization problem and guiding the optimizer. Our results indicate that test participants successfully identified effective structures that reduced the effective dimensionality of the search space by 2 to 4 times compared to unstructured approaches, while also yielding higher final scores on benchmark tasks.

The application of the AMPT model to Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=2.76$ Ter, covering centralities from 1% to 80% in the most central events, yields an average multiplicity of $3990 \pm 10$ charged particles within $|\eta|<0.8$ units, demonstrating consistency with ALICE experimental data regarding pT spectra and integrated yields for various particle species. The model accurately reproduces the dependence of elliptic flow ($v_2$) and triangular flow ($v_3$) on transverse momentum and the scalar transverse momentum for protons, deuterons, helium-3 ions, and various charged hadron categories. Furthermore, predictions for identified hadron non-fl correlations, specifically the $v_2$ value of $0.10 \pm 0.01$ at $p_T$ of $2$ Ge/c, align well with recent alace measurements.

Linked Data holds the potential to transform how users interact with and utilize information across the Web; however, this realization is currently hindered by the inherent limitations of Linked Data quality. Consequently, this study presents a framework designed to enhance the data quality of Linked Resources by integrating them with knowledge graphs. Specifically, our framework employs a set of data quality measures to identify areas for improvement, utilizing a data integration approach to resolve these issues. This approach relies on a semantic matching component that leverages the DBpedia ontology to facilitate the process. To validate our methodology, we conducted an experiment using a subset of DBpedia containing 1,000 entities drawn from the movie domain. Our findings indicate that our framework successfully enhances data quality measures, particularly regarding cardinality, distinct values, and completeness.

In many practical scenarios involving stochastic processes, maximum likelihood estimation is often the preferred method for parameter inference. However, this approach can be computationally demanding, prone to bias, and susceptible to overfitting. This paper introduces a novel nonparametric estimator that approximates the likelihood function with arbitrary precision. Furthermore, it demonstrates that this new method yields consistent estimates matching the asymptotic properties of the standard likelihood estimator.

We present new optical and near-infrared spectroscopic data for the Seyfert galaxy NGC 4151, obtained from the Keck I Telescope, the Gemini North Telescope, and the Magellan Telescopes. This dataset allows us to refine the geometry and physical properties of the broad-line region (BLR) and the dusty torus surrounding the supermassive black hole. We determined the black hole mass to be $4.0^{+1.0}_{-0.3} \times 10^7 M_{\odot}$, a value consistent with previous estimates. Our analysis reveals that electron temperatures in the BLR span a range of $1.0 \times 10^5$ K to $3.0 \times 10^5$ K, while the dust torus exhibits a significantly lower temperature between $150$ K and $300$ K. Furthermore, we find that the distribution of electron temperatures in the BLR aligns well with predictions from standard ionization models, whereas torus dust temperature distributions are better explained by a two-component heating mechanism. Finally, we discuss the implications of these results for AGN unification schemes.

The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has become widespread, yet IoT application security remains underdeveloped. Software vendors face the challenge of testing applications across a vast array of device configurations, which can be time-consuming and difficult to manage. To address this, we introduce a novel framework designed to automatically generate IoT device configurations for testing purposes. This framework employs a strategy that systematically varies both individual and interacting parameters, streamlining the creation of diverse virtual device setups.

Current approaches to traffic scene generation often rely on modifying images from existing datasets, resulting in unrealistic roadways, infrastructure, or traffic signals that fail to capture the diversity of genuine traffic situations. In contrast, our work introduces a method that synthesizes entire driving scenes by integrating real camera feeds with virtual elements like roads, curbs, and signs. Leveraging the diversity inherent in actual data, our model learns the statistical correlations between visual features of these virtual components and the surrounding image context, enabling it to render scenes that are highly diverse and closely mirror real-world conditions. Furthermore, we develop a novel curriculum learning algorithm that progressively refines scene generation quality by gradually increasing the complexity of image features utilized for synthesis. Experimental results indicate that our approach produces scenes exhibiting greater diversity than those created by prior methods, while also enhancing the generation of specific features such as curbs and signs.
We examine the Ising model within a Cayley tree of order three and discover new weakly periodic measures that correspond to normal subgroups of index 2 from the tree-Cayley Cayley group's.

Developing numerical schemes for time-dependent partial differential equations is a challenging endeavor, as it requires balancing numerous factors to achieve accuracy, efficiency, and stability. When designing a new scheme, a critical priority is establishing rigorous convergence analysis to verify that numerical solutions approach the true exact solution as discretization parameters diminish. This document presents the derivation of a new, implicit second-order finite difference method applied to a specific class of second-order second-parabolic integro-differential equations featuring convolution integral terms with non-local kernels. We demonstrate the convergence of this proposed approach to the exact solution at a rate of $O(\Delta t^2 + h^2)$, where $\Delta t$ denotes the temporal step size and $h$ represents the spatial step size. Finally, we include several numerical experiments to validate the theoretical findings and illustrate the practical efficacy of this method.

We have conducted three-dimensional radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations of a 10^5 M_sun star cluster in low-metallicity environments (Z = 0.02 Z_sun) to investigate dust evolution within superbubbles generated by supernovae. Our analysis indicates that dust grain growth occurs at a rate of approximately 1000 times faster in these low-metallicity superbubbles during their early evolutionary phase (t < 10^5 years) compared to the interstellar medium surrounding them. This rapid growth is primarily driven by the interaction of intense radiation fields with highly ionized gas. Conversely, at later stages (t > 10^5 years), dust destruction becomes the dominant process, resulting in a destruction rate roughly 10 times faster than the growth rate.

This work addresses the challenge of identifying distant targets beyond the range of conventional object detection algorithms, which typically stop around 50 meters due to diminishing lidar point density. Relying on a depth-from-lidar framework, the proposed method first segments the scene into planes and subsequently isolates objects by differentiating between the ground and far-field targets. To achieve this, it utilizes a graph-based approach that leverages geometric properties of strong reflective planes found in distant areas. Furthermore, to distinguish roads from other surfaces, the method employs a newly defined metric called the Van Hove angle, which leverages epipolar geometry principles. Experimental results from both real-world lidar data and the KITTI dataset validate the efficacy of the proposed solution.

This study examines chemical reactions by modeling them as trajectories on the potential energy surface. To achieve this, we introduce a newly derived expression for the Rényi relative entropy between path measures. Utilizing this formula, we calculate the Rényi relative entropy along with other related quantities specifically for the Lennard-Jones reaction. Through these computations, we gain deeper insights into the nature of chemical reactions.

Non-rigid registration stands as a critical technology for analyzing soft tissue changes in medical procedures, with a primary application being the tracking of anatomical structures. This study introduces a new approach to registering abdominal organs by integrating spatio-temporal constraints. The method relies on the assumption that an organ's surface maintains a consistent distance from its centroid over time, implemented as a Gaussian potential energy function. Additionally, the model incorporates temporal constraints to account for periodic movement patterns, utilizing a Hooke's law-based spring mechanism connecting current and expected surface positions. To handle multi-cycle data, the formulation utilizes a multi-penalty representation. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that the proposed method effectively suppresses folding artifacts in registered liver videos compared to existing methods.

This paper investigates the energy-momentum tensor's conformal matter collineations within the context of non-degenerate, spherically symmetric, and static spacetimes. We establish that such spacetimes always possess at least one independent conformal matter collineation. For the specific case where the tensor is trace-free, the symmetry group is at least two-dimensional and includes at least one independent conformal Killing vector field. In the general scenario, the symmetry group is at least three-dimensional, containing at least two independent conformal matter collineations. Additionally, we identify specific conditions under which the group reaches its maximum possible dimension of four, with all associated generating vector fields being explicitly calculated.

Precise motion vector estimation is crucial for effectively segmenting dynamic 3D environments into static background, dynamic objects, and unclassified regions. This study introduces a novel dense motion estimation technique grounded in a fully differentiable optical flow framework that incorporates multi-view geometric constraints. By integrating these constraints, the proposed approach enhances the accuracy of the recovered motion vectors and simultaneously mitigates estimation ambiguities. To achieve this multi-view geometry integration within differentiable frameworks, we utilize multi-view reprojection errors as a loss function, employing a stochastic gradient descent optimizer to perform joint refinement of both motion and depth estimates. Furthermore, to resolve the circular dependency often found in current loop-based refinement methods, we directly optimize an end-to-end differentiable pipeline. Evaluation across both synthetic datasets and real-world scenarios demonstrates that the proposed system outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in generating high-precision motion vectors necessary for robust dynamic segmentation.

Although Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) have achieved remarkable success in various domains, Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer superior energy and computational efficiency by leveraging temporal coding and sparse activation. A key challenge in converting ANNs to SNNs lies in preserving performance during conversion, particularly given the limitations of current optimization techniques. This study introduces a new learning algorithm that utilizes sparse connections to boost convergence speed without sacrificing accuracy. Our method applies evolutionary strategies to optimize the connectivity matrices of SNNs, thereby yielding an effective sparse configuration. To validate the approach, we trained a convolutional sparse SNN classifier on the CIFAR-10 dataset via deep backpropagation. The resulting model reached a test accuracy of 74.3%, surpassing that of its fully connected counterpart by 0.8%. The accompanying source code is available at https://github.com/AmirHosseinGhazanfari/CSNN-Evolutionary.

Our analysis examines spin polarization across various temperatures and field strengths, specifically highlighting the impact of these interactions and the field itself on the average inter-quark separation and the system's energy density, temperature, and entropy density at specific average filling factors. Our findings highlight that both the degree of spin polarization and the specified thermodynamic parameters are sensitive to variations in filling factor. Furthermore, we determined that both the spin polarization degree and the specified thermodynamic properties are sensitive to changes in field strength. Additionally, we observed that increasing field strength increases the spin polarization degree and the specified thermodynamic properties, while decreasing inter-quark separation, energy density, temperature, and entropy density. A graph $G$ exhibits the Perfect-Matching-Hamiltonian (PMH) property if every one of its perfect matchings can be paired with another perfect matching such that their union forms a Hamiltonian cycle. This paper demonstrates that the PMH-property holds for complete multipartite graphs where each part contains an even number of vertices. Additionally, it generalizes a prior result by D. Rall regarding the local independence of the square of a cycle. Finally, the paper derives a formula to determine the local independence of the square of any tree that possesses an even order.

The Bunyakovsky Conjecture asserts that any irreducible quadratic polynomial with integer coefficients, which assumes positive values at zero and possesses integer discriminant, generates an infinite sequence of prime numbers when evaluated. Assuming the validity of this conjecture, we establish the existence of quadratic fields containing sequences that are completely multiplicative and contain arbitrarily long linear recurrence subsequences within them.

System call auditing is a fundamental security practice for software, yet filtering excessive irrelevant invocations remains challenging. This paper introduces Timeloops, a novel, trace-driven technique that leverages application execution history to identify useful system calls. Unlike static analysis methods, Timeloops avoids false negatives, while surpassing heuristic-driven approaches by offering greater precision. The study utilizes the popular Go language to implement this solution, featuring a lightweight interpreter that executes partial programs containing only relevant system calls. Extensive testing with Timeloops across 14 diverse system functions processing various microservice tasks processed 2.66 million system calls with a recall of 99.99%, filtering 93.4% of redundant calls. The study also developed a static analysis tool that analyzes compiled binaries to automatically extract these necessary calls from execution histories. Executing this extraction logic on 14 Go microservices resulted in the identification of an average 90.9% of system calls, with a 98.2% success rate.

The introduction of right-handed neutrinos into the Standard Model enables the acquisition of minuscule neutrino masses via the seesaw mechanism and serves as a viable source for dark matter. This study examines the stability of dark matter within an extended Standard Model incorporating a complex scalar dark matter candidate that couples to both Higgs and right-handed neutrinos through both Yukawa and quartic self-interactions. We perform a thorough investigation into the parameter space, delineating the regions consistent with current experimental data. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of quartic self-interactions on dark matter stability and its sensitivity to direct detection constraints. Our findings reveal that while these quartic couplings can expand the area of the parameter space compatible with existing data, they simultaneously enhance the scattering cross-section, thereby reducing the likelihood of compatibility with direct detection experiments.

This study introduces a Poisson multi-Bernoulli mixture (PMBM) filter that utilizes a grid-based trait probability density instead of the conventional Gaussian mixture (GAM) approximation. By establishing a one-to-one correspondence between mixture components and Gauss-Hermite quadrature nodes, the proposed method derives closed-form relations for updating the Reed-Shepp-Bertozzi-Ahmed (RSBMA) filter and the multi-Bernoulli mixture (MBM) filter components. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that this approach yields equivalent tracking accuracy to the RSBMA filter while significantly decreasing the number of required trajectories. Furthermore, this method effectively mitigates the excessive target association errors often observed in the RSBMA filter when targets originate from the same location.

This work investigates the null controllability within a population dynamics framework subject to interior degenerate diffusion. Initially, we establish a novel Carleman estimate applicable to the auxiliary dual problem, which subsequently enables the derivation of the key observability inequality required to demonstrate the existence of a control function for the primary system capable of driving the population to total extinction within a finite timeframe within the diffusion domain. Secondly, we address a secondary scenario involving a specific source term and succeed in proving an exact controllability result.

Soccer is a globally popular team sport where players and fans alike analyze game dynamics to evaluate and predict outcomes. While existing research has focused on extracting statistical patterns from historical data, there remains a need to understand how game states influence optimal decision-making in real-time. This study addresses that gap by analyzing game scenarios through the lens of a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to derive and validate critical insights about soccer strategy. Specifically, we demonstrate that a goal probability threshold exists which dictates a shift in the optimal action during pivotal moments of a match. Furthermore, we analyze the factors influencing this threshold and confirm through empirical scenarios that game states can drive significant variations in strategic choices.

Full waveform inversion (FWI) serves as a cornerstone technique in seismic imaging for subsurface characterization. Although recent advancements in deep learning have yielded promising results in various domains, their integration into waveform modeling remains limited. To address this, we introduce Wavefield Reconstruction Inversion (WRI), a novel deep learning framework designed to accelerate full waveform inversion (FWI). The methodology operates on the premise that the deep learning model is pre-trained to generate a high-frequency wavefield from a low-frequency, smoothed initial estimate. This refined field is subsequently utilized for the acceleration step within the inversion loop. The approach is grounded in a high-frequency asymptotic theory, which posits that a smoothed, low-frequency approximation of the true high-frequency wavefield is adequate for accurate objective function evaluation. We validate the efficacy of the proposed method through both synthetic and field-based experiments, demonstrating that it achieves a significantly faster convergence rate compared to traditional FWI.

We propose an optical nonreciprocal resonator design based on a single mechanical mode, where reciprocity is broken by applying a pump to create quantum squeezing in the reservoir. This arrangement enables optical isolation within a minor frequency detuning from the resonant state, with a magnitude that increases as mechanical photons are reduced. We further demonstrate that this mechanism is resilient to mechanical dissipation and demonstrates efficacy even when the mechanical frequency is significantly lower than the resonator's frequency. Our findings offer a viable strategy for integrating mechanical components into photonic architectures, facilitating the miniaturization of systems requiring both mechanical interaction and optical nonreciprocity.

Additionally, optical observations conducted with the 2.0-m Liverpool Telescope revealed a bright, point-like source with a spectral type of B3V, which aligns spatially with the X-ray position. This study presents a new extension of the classic Lotka-Volterra competition model to incorporate immigration, allowing for dynamic entry of species into the system. We derive analytical conditions determining whether an immigrating species can successfully invade and persist. Furthermore, we develop a computational algorithm designed to map out the parameter regions where simultaneous species coexistence occurs within this enhanced framework.

The observation of the Sun's diurnal motion served as a daily reminder of the rotation of the Earth around its axis, a fact that was evident to classical Islamic scholars, even if they did not always explicitly articulate it. This natural phenomenon, along with the stars' diurnal motion, functioned as a fundamental basis for Islamic astronomy and timekeeping. Consequently, the development of astrolabes and related instruments was driven by the need to determine prayer times and the Qibla direction.

This study examines a device-to-device (D2D) communication pair situated within a cellular network, with the objective of enhancing direct link reliability. To achieve this, an Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) is implemented, enabling the D0 communications to leverage either the direct path or an IRS-mediated reflected path. The core objective involves optimizing the system by jointly configuring the power allocation for both transmission links and the phase shifts of the IRS. Specifically, the authors formulate a non-convex optimization problem designed to maximize the multiplexing gain of the D2D pair. Analytical closed-form solutions are derived for the optimal power allocation and the corresponding multiplexing gain under various channel conditions. Furthermore, numerical simulations are conducted to validate the proposed approach and assess its performance.

Two-dimensional (2D) Laser Doppler Vibrometry (LDV) serves as a powerful analytical tool for evaluating how samples react to diverse external stimuli, particularly when integrated with automated sample scanning. This study introduces a method to determine the optimal scanning path and associated parameters using a Genetic Algorithm (GA). The efficacy of this approach is validated through an experiment involving a cantilever beam, where the algorithm successfully identified the axis parallel to the beam's longitudinal direction and matched the measured resonant frequencies against established reference values.

Although current interest in programmable electrostatic phase plates (PEPP) is driven by the need for on-site correction of chromatic aberrations in Transmission Electron Microscopes, there is also potential to utilize these plates to improve spatial resolution. This can be achieved by correcting spherical aberration through the strategic arrangement of multiple annular segments. This study examines the theoretical limits of such PEPPs, specifically analyzing the trade-off between the number of rings and the achievable resolution. The analysis indicates that a phase plate with three rings can match the resolution of an instrument with perfectly corrected spherical aberration, provided the defocus is optimized. Furthermore, if the defocus is held constant, a plate design with five rings can achieve a resolution within 10% of that from an ideal instrument.

In this study, we introduce DiPoCo, a new dataset designed for predicting suitable responses in dialogues through cooperative task execution. This corpus comprises 28,000+ dialogue pairs, where each pair consists of a multi-turn user intention and a corresponding system response. We establish a new evaluation metric, Instruction Relevance, to assess the semantic similarity between the user intention and system response. Our experiments indicate that contextual information is crucial for predicting appropriate system responses; we further report baseline results using both our proposed method and several state-of-the-art models.

This study introduces a novel place recognition system for autonomous driving that utilizes 3D LiDAR data, employing a supervised learning approach to achieve high accuracy and robustness. The core of the proposed method is a deep learning network trained to generate a globally consistent, compact, and semantically meaningful representation from raw LiDAR inputs. The training dataset consists of location pairs gathered from large-scale driving benchmarks, specifically the Natural Driving Dataset (NDD). The global consistency of these descriptors is established through a global alignment phase utilizing a learned transformation model. The feasibility of the proposed framework is validated on the NDD, demonstrating its superior performance.

Cloud virtual machine video transcoding represents a viable solution for addressing the high computational demands of video processing, enabling the distribution of tasks across multiple machines to significantly reduce operational expenses. Nevertheless, the effectiveness of this approach relies heavily on various factors, including task decomposition strategies, scheduling algorithms, and network latency. This study introduces a novel video transcoding framework designed to enhance the efficiency of such processes on cloud infrastructure. By decomposing tasks into finer granularities and utilizing lock-free mechanisms for concurrent access, the proposed method facilitates task parallelism and improves overall processing speed. Furthermore, the research evaluates the proposed solution's performance by comparing it against a sequential transcoding approach across different cloud configurations.

At low energy scales, electrons within doped Dirac semimetals behave as massless Dirac fermions. In this study, we examine the thermal properties of a three-dimensional (3D) system of 3D system of massless Dirac fermions experiencing short-range disorder, utilizing the self-consistent Born approximation. Our findings indicate that at sufficiently low temperatures, the specific heat capacity $C_v$ scales linearly with $T$, while the electrical conductivity $\sigma$ follows a $T^2$ relationship. These results contrast with previous predictions from the renormalization group approach, which suggested a $C_v \propto T^{2}$ scaling and $\sigma \propto T$ dependence. To address this discrepancy, we propose a theory positing that the self-consistent Born approximation inadequately captures the dynamical self-energy required to describe both thermal and transport phenomena accurately in these regimes.

Human conversational speech involves numerous critical elements, such as semantic content, temporal flow, emotional tone, and pragmatic context. However, current research primarily concentrates on lower-level features like pronunciation and intonation, largely overlooking higher-order aspects like emotion and pragmatics. To address this gap, we present SpeechGen, a user-centered framework designed to automatically generate high-quality paragraphs for speech synthesis. Our approach leverages a two-stage architecture: first, it employs a user model to infer emotions and pragmatic nuances from written input, followed by a conditional neural network that creates speech by integrating these inferences with the text. Experiments across two datasets demonstrate that SpeechGen substantially outperforms baseline methods in assessing both emotional accuracy and pragmatic correctness.

We derive explicit formulas characterizing the spectral and orbital stability for solitary wave solutions to the solitary U(1)-symmetric Klein-Gordon equation with one spatial dimension and an anharmonic interaction term. These solutions are obtained by applying a stability analysis to a solitary wave that satisfies a Euler-Lagrange type eigenvalue problem with an eigenvalue parameter in the non-linear term.

"Although the standard No-Hair Theorem for scalar-tensor theories forbids No-Hairs around static black holes, this study demonstrates that No-Hairs can form around static black holes in the Higgs-Portal model when the No-Hair field possesses a self-interaction term and the theory exhibits spontaneous symmetry breaking. Specifically, a distinct No-Hair solution—the "cored No-Hair"—carrying a non-vanishing field value directly at the black hole horizon is identified as energetically stable under specific conditions. This cored No-Hair solution features a mass that is lower than the sum of the masses of a standard No-Hair solution and the equivalent mass of the trapped matter, indicating its superior efficiency. Furthermore, the Higgs-Portal model allows for the coexistence of at least two different static black hole solutions: one where the Higgs field is trapped (the "hairy" solution) and another where it is not (the "no-hairy" solution). The presence of these multiple states suggests that the "No-Hair" theorem for singlet scalar-tensor theories is contingent upon the specific structure of the coupling between the No-Hair field and the Higgs sector.

We investigate the evolution of a cyclic cosmos that begins with a Big Bang singularity, transitions into a big crunch singularity, and repeats indefinitely, undergoing infinite cycles. By employing a Hubble radius as the infrared cutoff within holographic dark energy (HDE) models, we analyze whether such a universe can support a true singularity-free bounce. Our findings indicate that a true bounce is unattainable in cyclic cosmologies when the Hubble radius defines the infrared boundary. Consequently, the standard HDE cyclic model, which relies on an accelerating expansion phase followed by a transition to contraction, becomes incompatible with a bouncing universe scenario. Furthermore, we explore the feasibility of a non-cyclic universe that transitions from a singularity-free initial singularity to a singularity-free final singularity (a direct transition from initial to final states without cycling). Our analysis reveals that a successful transition from a singularity-free initial singularity to a singularity-free final singularity is unattainable when utilizing the Hubble radius as the infrared cutoff.

A bond scattering matrix is defined for any graph $G$ possessing a unitary bond scattering matrix, which ensures that $G$ is lossless. We demonstrate that a graph $F$ constitutes a spectral cover of graph $G$ if and only if there exists a subgroup of unitary bond scattering matrices enabling the lossless embedding of $F$ into the bond scattering matrix of $G$. Leveraging this characterization, we identify numerous graphs that admit multiple distinct lossless realizations within some unitary bond scattering matrix. Furthermore, we establish a direct correspondence between the spectra of graphs embedded within a specific spectral cover and those contained within the associated subgroup of unitary bond scattering matrices. Finally, we present a computational procedure designed to locate pairs consisting of a unitary bond scattering matrix and a set of constituent graphs, specifically for graphs $G$ whose bond scattering matrix has a distinct spectrum.

We establish the results demonstrating that for specific finite, non-abelian, p-ramified extensions F of Q with Galois groups isomorphic to A4, A5, or S4, the ring of integers of F remains free over its relevant order within the rational group algebra Q[G].

Contemporary techniques for identifying diachronic semantic shift rely heavily on contextualized representations, which are susceptible to the "temporal aggregation problem." This issue arises when merging word senses from different eras into a single static vector, thereby potentially masking genuine changes in meaning. We introduce Temporal-Projected Contextualized (TPC) embeddings as a solution that preserves the temporal integrity of these vectors. Our approach projects contextualized usages of a target word into a dedicated, time-localized subspace, creating an aggregated vector that remains confined strictly to a specific time window. We evaluate our method against existing contextual-based identification and detection frameworks, utilizing English Wikipedia data to demonstrate that TPC embeddings significantly enhance embedding quality for semantic drift detection. Furthermore, we examine English Wikipedia and Wiktionary datasets to identify instances of English drift successfully detected by TPC, which outperforms current contextualized methods.

The mass and spin of black holes in Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) can be determined by analyzing their electromagnetic spectra across multiple wavelengths, a technique that is particularly effective for nearby objects. This study presents a novel method for estimating the mass and spin of nearby black holes in X-ray binaries by utilizing the optical spectrum to infer the ultraviolet (UV) spectrum, which is otherwise obscured by interstellar dust. The approach relies on the tight correlation between the optical-UV spectral energy distribution (SED) and the shape of the broad Balmer emission line. By modeling the line-shape formation using the Monte Carlo code `mcsl`, we can reconstruct the underlying SED from observed optical line profiles. This technique is applicable to both single and broadened double-peaked lines, provided the broadening mechanism is understood. We demonstrate the method's efficacy using synthetic spectra generated from the `GEOCAN` radiative transfer code, which simulates the line-shape formation in the Broad Line Region (BLR) of an AGN. Our results indicate that this technique can recover spin and mass estimates within uncertainties of approximately 10\% and 20\%, respectively.

Interkinetic nuclear migration (IKNM), characterized by nuclei moving rhythmically between apical and basal positions in response to cell cycle transitions, serves as a fundamental mechanism in early brain development. While the drivers for nuclear movement during this phase have been extensively documented, the factors regulating the precise timing of nuclear migration relative to the cell cycle remain less clear. This study investigates IKNM in the embryonic mouse retina using the cell cycle reporter EdU, combined with three-dimensional (3D) image reconstruction and analysis. The findings reveal that nuclei incorporate EdU during both S phases of the cell cycle, yet nuclei remain stationary while EdU accumulates in the developing retina. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the duration of G1 and G2 phases varies significantly depending on the nuclear position: G1 and G2 periods are prolonged at the retinal base compared to the apex. These results indicate that asymmetric cell cycle timing regulates the rhythm of IKNM in the early mouse retina.

Various image processing applications, including video compressed sensing and color image demosaicing, involve extracting data from coded representations via a process called encoded domain sampling. These tasks rely on code pattern designs that facilitate the reconstruction of images from sparse data. This study introduces a new approach to encoded sampling, specifically for applications like those mentioned, by utilizing a random projection matrix as the code pattern. We demonstrate that this method guarantees a stable, robust basis for sparse representation of code-harbored data through the application of the Restricted Isometry Property (RIP). Furthermore, we validate the efficacy of this proposed pattern across two specific use cases: a video compressed sensing scenario employing separable sparse transforms, and an error-optimized demosaicing process in color image applications.

We present a hydrodynamic framework designed to analyze the flow dynamics of inactive (passive) and active incompressible polar active matter subjected to quenched disorder. By applying a coarse-grained approach, we determine the corresponding coarse-grained stress tensor and the associated stochastic advection-diffusion equation for the vorticity field. Our analysis reveals that such fluids exhibit non-monotonic diffusive behavior across a broad spectrum of interaction strengths and activity levels. Specifically, weak disorder induces a transition from normal diffusion to superdiffusion, whereas strong disorder generates a superseding regime of superdiffusion characterized by negative effective diffusion coefficients; this second stage is followed by the recovery of standard diffusion. The phenomenon of superdiffusion with Coefficients is attributed to the interplay between self-advection and diffusive processes, a mechanism that persists regardless of whether the system is active or inactive.

This study presents a security analysis of the research infrastructure network at the University of Toronto, Carleton University, and the National Center for Supercomputing Applications (NCSA). Data was gathered via passive packet capture across the nodes of this communication backbone. Subsequent examination of network traffic protocols and simulations utilizing the empirical dataset reveal that 20% of the nodes are susceptible to the "On-path Node" attack, a scenario where a significant portion of the network traffic remains exposed to interception. Furthermore, the analysis demonstrates that a network controller can intercept traffic from a substantial segment of the network by establishing connections with only a minimal number of nodes.

This novel class of liquids, termed the "exceptionally repulsive liquid," is characterized by a unique singularity in its electronic structure known as the "exceptional van Hove singularity" (EFHS). This singularity is distinct from the traditional repulsive type due to its unique origin, which involves the interplay between interaction effects and the geometry of the Fermi surface. The presence of EFHS is a direct consequence of the interaction-induced modification of the Fermi surface, which is not present in non-interacting systems. This paper details the design, construction, and initial performance of the Spallation Neutron Source (SND) muon-neutron detector, a specialized instrument intended for precise measurements of the time correlation between cosmic-ray muons and induced spallation neutons. The detector comprises a 1,000-ton water Cherenkov tank instrumented with 1,152 photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) and features a 20-ton active scintillator sub-detector. Strategically positioned 100 meters downwind of the Fermilab Main Injector, the apparatus captures a target flux of approximately 1000 muons per kiloton-second, with a corresponding neutron rate of roughly 100 neutrons per kiloton-second. The design ensures a timing resolution of 100 nanoseconds, enabling the detection of neutron events within a 1-microsecond window following muon passage. The report concludes with a description of the data acquisition system and the calibration methodology employed.

Space-based transit missions like TESS have been highly successful in identifying thousands of transiting exoplanets, yet their ability to determine precise masses and characterize planetary interiors depends on complementary radial velocity (RV) observations. This study utilizes the extensive, high-precision RV data from the HARPS-NORdical Extended Survey (HARPS-NEXT) to assess the suitability of ground-based RV surveys for validating and refining TESS targets. We conducted a statistical analysis of 1,000 randomly selected TESS targets, each containing a single transiting planet candidate, to determine the fraction yielding detectable RV signals under various signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) thresholds. Our findings indicate that approximately 18% of these targets produce detectable RV signals at an SNR of 10, rising to 38% at an SNR of 5. Furthermore, we evaluated the fraction of systems containing multi-planet architectures capable of generating detectable perturbations. Results suggest that 20% of systems host at least one additional planet detectable at an SNR of 10, while 41% contain such planets detectable at an SNR of 5. These statistics provide a statistical framework for prioritizing TESS targets for future mass confirmation and multi-planet detection via RV methods.

Extracting text from pictures of identification cards is essential for automating text-based verification processes, such as checking for spelling errors or validating data formats. However, traditional optical character recognition (OCR) methods often yield subpar results when processing curved surfaces. To address this limitation, this study introduces a technique that converts images of ID cards into three-dimensional representations, enabling accurate structure-aware text recognition. The proposed approach utilizes a deep learning-based algorithm to determine the geometric characteristics of the card-issuing machine, thereby reconstructing the three-dimensional shape of the card through surface mapping. Subsequently, kitting text detection and correction algorithms generate straightened text lines from the images for final character recognition. Experiments conducted on 1,000 images of Chinese driver's licenses demonstrate that this approach successfully extracts text with a 98.4% success rate.

We simulate the ground state of a Harmonic Quantum Oscillator subjected to constant forces via discrete time evolution. In this model, position and momentum are discrete, and momentum updates occur in time steps according to $p \mapsto p + F\Delta t$. Specifically, we examine a system where a particle is confined to move on a ring with discrete coordinates $x \in \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ and $\mathbb{Z}$-valued momentum $p \in \mathbb{Z}$. The potential $V(x)$ is constructed by linearly interpolating values $V(x_j)$ defined at discrete points $x_j \in \{0, \dots, N-1\}$, creating a periodic structure on the ring. Our findings indicate that under specific update rules for an initially broad initial state spread over $x$ and $p$, the state evolution mirrors that of a continuous harmonic oscillator. We validate these results through experiments on a trapped-ion platform.

The rotation of small asteroids is influenced by the Yarkovsky-O'Keefe-Radzievskii-Paddack (YORP) effect, which stems from the absorption and re-emission of solar radiation. This phenomenon is notoriously difficult to model accurately, and while its impact is significant for YORP-driven evolutionary changes in rotation states, it remains challenging to verify through direct observation. To address this discrepancy, we developed a statistical framework designed to extract YORP effect parameters from sparse and noisy data regarding the rotation states of small asteroids. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through a simulation study and subsequently applied it to data from the Near-Earth Asteroid Tracking (NEAT) survey. Our analysis identified 11 Near-Earth asteroids (NEAs) exhibiting statistically significant YORP effects, a finding that aligns well with simulation outcomes.

Political discourse on social media platforms like Twitter has become increasingly prominent, often sparking intense debates that drive user engagement. This study examines the characteristics of political tweets posted by users during discussions concerning the 2016 US Presidential Election, analyzing data from a comprehensive collection of over 1.5 billion messages. By leveraging a topic model to categorize the dataset, the research identifies distinct clusters of political-related activity. The findings indicate that these tweets exhibit greater negativity and higher levels of urgency compared to non-political content, with such traits becoming even more pronounced during periods of intense debate. Furthermore, the study highlights a cluster of "comprehensive discussions"—groups of interlinked, contextually relevant dialogues that sustain engagement for extended durations. Finally, the analysis explores the nature of interactions surrounding these dialogues, offering insights into the broader dynamics of political communication within the Twitter ecosystem.

The authors demonstrate that any subgroup of a group consisting of homeomorphisms which keep a compact surface's boundary stationary, provided these homeomorphisms act with sufficient transitivity within the surface's interior, lacks Roelcke precompactness when equipped with the topology derived from the compact-open topology.

The discovery and characterization of exoplanets, along with the study of their host stars' stellar envelopes, cores, and internal structures, rely heavily on precise photometric and spectroscopic data. Consequently, accurate photometric and spectroscopic observations are fundamental to advancing exoplanet science and understanding stars. This paper presents the results of a photometric analysis conducted on the TESS Target List, utilizing the 1.54-m TCS telescope located at the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan (NAOJ). The study processed TESS data to generate light curves for 1,100,000 TESS targets, achieving a photometric precision of 0.0015 mag for bright TESS sources. This dataset has been made accessible via a dedicated website.

Line waves emerge at the interface of dual electromagnetic metasurfaces, representing a novel type of wavefront characterized by confinement within a narrow plane parallel to the interface and propagation along that interface. This study investigates the potential of end-to-end neural automatic speech recognition (ASR) through fully automatic, multimodal training that leverages vast amounts of unprocessed web data. Experimental results indicate that this approach yields a 15% relative reduction in Word Error Rate (WER) on the Librispeech test set when compared to standard audio-based ASR models.

Inter-orbital coupling represents a fundamental concept in photonic lattices, defined by the exchange of photons between different orbital modes within a single lattice site. This study introduces a novel, experimentally accessible mechanism to generate such coupling via the rotation of uniaxia anisotropic optical lattices around the propagation axis. The theoretical framework is substantiated by a demonstration using hot atomic vapors, where the rotation induces a transformation in the atomic energy levels' spatial configuration relative to the atoms. This alteration results in the generation of synthetic gauge fields for light, thereby facilitating robust inter-orbital coupling. The proposed approach offers a versatile and practical route for engineering inter-site inter-orbital coupling in photonic systems, with potential applications in the development of advanced photonic devices.

The $\Omega^-$, a triply heavy $sss$ baryon, serves as a unique testing ground for QCD and the investigation of new physics. This study employs the lattice QCD framework to determine the $\Omega^-$ magnetic dipole moment and its coupling to two vector mesons, specifically $VV$ states ($VV=\rho\rho, \omega\omega, KK$). Our calculations utilize $2+1$ flavor twisted-mass cloven Wilson quark actions on gauge configurations generated by the MILC collaboration, featuring physical quark masses and an inverse lattice spacing of $am=0.07$. We extract the $\Omega^-$ vector coupling via the energy spectrum of an $\Omega^-$ placed alongside $VV$ pairs. Our results yield a $\Omega^-$ magnetic dipole moment of $\mu_{\Omega^-} = 0.149(10)\, \mu_N$ and a renormalized $VV$ coupling of $g_{\Omega^-VV}^R = 0.000(10)$.

Air transmission of viruses within enclosed environments depends intricately on the interplay between turbulent airflow and the nucleation and growth of virus-carrying aerosols. This study examines airflow patterns and the transmission of SARS-CoV-2 in a typical conference room using Large Eddy Simulation (LES) coupled with a condensation module. The LES framework integrates an Smagorinsky-Lilly subgrid-scale model with a dynamic model to assess their respective impacts on viral exposure for seated occupants. Simulation results indicate that dynamic subgrid-scale models more accurately capture the movement of exhaled droplets and nuclei, potentially leading to underestimates of exposure when using the Smagorinsky-Lilly model. Furthermore, the research demonstrates how airflow dynamics and respiratory droplet behavior influence infection risk under various conditions, including occupant activities, mask usage, ventilation strategies, and environmental humidity levels.

Driven by the proposal to utilize x-ray and optical lasers to simulate atomic physics in extreme conditions, we examine the birefringent scattering of x-rays within intense laser fields. This phenomenon arises from the polarization-dependent refractive indices of light in matter, which, when combined with polarization rotation induced by the laser field, results in a significant change in polarization. We demonstrate that this effect reaches its maximum when a visible laser aligns perpendicular to the x-ray beam, generating a strong "optical grating" that causes scattering angles on the order of microradians. Furthermore, we show that this setup functions as a polarimeter capable of measuring circular polarization fractions exceeding 1%, a capability that could be instrumental for future polarimetry in multi-photon processes.

This study examines information-theoretic authentication at the physical layer when the adversary possesses prior access to the channel and aims to deceive a benign receiver by substituting a transmitted message $M$ with an impostor message $M'$. The proposed attack succeeds if the receiver's decoded message matches the tampered one ($\hat{M} = M'$) rather than the original ($\hat{M} \neq M'$). We demonstrate that authentication is feasible if the channel exhibits a memory effect, allowing the legitimate sender to embed a secret watermark into the transmission. This watermark enables the receiver to verify the integrity of the message. Conversely, we prove that if the adversary can replicate the channel's behavior perfectly, authentication becomes impossible. In response to this limitation, we introduce a new metric known as the "channel distinguishability" to quantify the degree of required channel memory.

Twisted transition metal dichalcogenide bilayers (TMDs) serve as a promising platform for investigating flat-band physics and strongly correlated electron behaviors. In this study, we introduce a low-energy effective Hamiltonian describing the physics of twisted bilayer TMDs. Our analysis reveals that when interlayer twist angles are near the valley degeneracy breaking point, these systems support low-damped, quasi-flat plasmon modes. Achieving both the suppression of electron scattering and maintaining low scattering rates requires simultaneously minimizing electron interactions and maintaining a high degree of crystalline perfection. These specific conditions enable the observation of quasi-flat plasmons at frequencies in the terahertz range.

Stars in the main sequence span a wide range of masses, from less than 0.5 solar masses ($M_{\odot}$) to over 100 solar masses ($M_{\odot}$). While lower-mass stars, such as our Sun, lose mass primarily through thermal coronal heating and magnetically driven processes, the mechanisms governing mass loss in very massive stars remain poorly understood. This study utilizes the radiation magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) code to investigate how magnetic fields influence mass loss in stars exceeding 10 solar masses ($M_{\odot}$). Our findings indicate that magnetic fields trigger a novel mass-loss mechanism driven by magnetocentrifugal instabilities, which can dominate over radiative line-driven loss. This effect is most pronounced in stars between 10 and 30 solar masses ($M_{\odot}$), where it generates a dense, high-velocity wind confined to a narrow equatorial stream. The resulting mass-loss rates are highly sensitive to stellar magnetic topology and can be orders of magnitude stronger than those predicted by standard radiative models. These outcomes align with recent observations of asymmetric outflows in massive stars and suggest that future population synthesis models must incorporate this mechanism to accurately reflect the real-world behavior of massive stellar evolution.

Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC) can be significantly amplified via the Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect (SOPE) at an interface with a material possessing strong SOC. This phenomenon arises from two mechanisms: intrinsic SOC induced by broken inversion symmetry within the bilayer system, and extrinsic SOC generated by interfacial scattering. While extrinsic SOC is sensitive to interface defects, this study demonstrates that extrinsic SOC can be deliberately tuned by engineering the interface electronic structure, specifically by integrating a monolayer of chiral adatoms onto the interface between a ferromagnetic (FM) film and a strong SOC layer. These chiral adatoms introduce a local chiral potential that induces spin-momentum locking in charge carriers within the adjacent FM film through extrinsic SOC. Consequently, the SOC of spins parallel to the FM magnetization increases, whereas SOC for antiparallel spins decreases. This modulation of SOC directly influences the spin precession dynamics of spin-polarized electrons within the FM layer, giving rise to a Spreading of Spin Precession (SSP) effect. SSP is defined as spin dephasing occurring even in the absence of spin-misalignment, driven by the coexistence of SOC values distinct for spins aligned and anti-aligned with the magnetization. This behavior is predicted to be observable in spin-hall magnetoresistance (SMR) measurements. Furthermore, the theoretical framework presented herein offers a viable route to engineer SMR in spin-valve configurations.

In this study, we present bounded state solutions for a fractional, one-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a double-well potential in fractional spatial derivatives of order $s \in (0,2)$. The potential takes the form $V(x) = \frac{1}{2}\kappa x^2 + \lambda x^p$, representing an anharmonic oscillator where $\kappa, \lambda,$ and $p$ are real parameters. By employing the shooting method, we derive approximate double-peaked solutions and analyze their properties under fractional derivative settings. Our findings indicate that fractional effects are governed by $\kappa$, $\lambda$, $p$, and $s$, with fractional influence intensifying as $s$ approaches 1. Furthermore, we observe that these solutions exhibit a tunneling phenomenon across the potential barrier.

We introduce a methodology for incorporating constraints on the Lipschitz constant into stochastic gradient descent (SGD) used for training neural networks. This approach ensures that the loss function adheres to specific smoothness requirements, which is crucial for safeguarding the robustness of models against adversarial inputs. Although this technique yields significant improvements in robustness, it comes with a trade-off of reduced accuracy. By regulating the smoothness of the loss function, we can mitigate the risk SGD takes of converging to poor local minima that exhibit high loss values but are surrounded by steep gradients. This effect is most evident in fully connected networks, where the proposed method achieves a better balance between robustness and accuracy compared to other techniques.

Sequential neural network models have demonstrated efficacy in predicting grammatical agreement across numerous languages, including English; however, their application to Basque remains untested. This study analyzes English and Basque agreement tasks to evaluate sequential neural networks, utilizing standard metrics and methods for comparison. Results indicate that while these models perform well on English agreement prediction, their performance degrades significantly for Basque. This disparity persists despite employing an expanded feature set and a more effective evaluation strategy than previous research, leading to the conclusion that the poor outcome for Basque stems from fundamental architectural limitations of sequential networks. Consequently, the authors propose a solution: a recurrence unit augmented with a connectionist layer, which successfully forecasts Basque agreement with high accuracy.

The highly eccentric orbit of the exoplanet Kepler-4139, with an eccentricity of $e=0.611\pm0.003$, causes a 14-fold variation in received stellar radiation, transitioning its equilibrium temperature between $330$ and $235$ K over one orbital period. This study evaluates the potential for liquid water on the rocky exoplanet by analyzing the spatial and temporal distribution of insolation, the planet's thermal inertia, and its orbital dynamics. Our findings indicate that liquid water can exist on the surface, particularly in equatorial regions, though the planet's overall habitability is heavily contingent upon its thermal properties and orbital characteristics. We further introduce a novel orbital metric, the orbital eccentricity timescale ($\tau_{orb}$), defined as the ratio of the orbital period to the timescale over which the semi-major axis changes. This parameter offers a robust method for characterizing radiation environments in systems undergoing orbital migration. For Kepler-4139, $\tau_{orb}$ is approximately $1.0\times10^5$ years, a value significantly shorter than the thermal relaxation time of roughly $1.0\times10^6$ years. This disparity suggests that rapid changes in stellar flux driven by orbital evolution likely dominate over the planet's thermal response.

Digital game adaptations have emerged as a strategy to boost motivation during repetitive motor exercises essential for rehabilitation. This study introduces "Tunnel Ball," a modified gaming variant designed to enhance upper limb motor function in stroke survivors. Participants engaged in five sessions of 20 minutes each, comprising five trials of two minutes per session. "Tunnel Ball" demonstrated superior performance compared to standard control exercises across all metrics, including total repetitions, movement speed, and consistency. Furthermore, the study found a significant positive link between the total number of movements executed and both speed and consistency scores. These outcomes indicate that adapted digital games offer a viable option for upper limb rehabilitation in stroke patients.

Users often harbor concerns about data gathering and personalization, which can hinder the efficacy of these systems. To address this, we conducted a study involving 1,000 participants who engaged in a news recommendation task. The experiment tested three recommendation approaches: one utilizing personal data, another avoiding the use of personal data, and a baseline. Results indicate that the majority of participants completed the task, yet a significant proportion expressed dissatisfaction with the collection of their personal information. Furthermore, users reported feeling more engaged and satisfied when the approach did not rely on personal data, challenging the notion that such methods reduce enjoyment. Finally, users demonstrated a marked preference for the condition that limited data to what was strictly necessary for task completion. These findings suggest a viable strategy for implementing data-efficient personalization in recommendation systems.

Centering Theory (Grosz et al., 1995) analyzes how the structural elements of conversation maintain coherence through successive utterances. This study introduces a novel, low-complexity adaptation of the Centering Framework specifically designed for the examination of corpus-wide text streams. We validate the approach using the Arabic Twitter Corpus, demonstrating that the model effectively identifies Centering violations within the data while also revealing systematic coherence failures inherent to the social media content.

We present a new definition for the upward planar representation of directed acyclic structures (DAGs), which we call UP-ADJ. In this model, the DAG's nodes are depicted as planar points, and its edges are drawn as upward non-intersecting curves. We demonstrate that deciding whether a DAG admits a UP-ADJ depiction is NP-complete. Furthermore, we identify specific subclasses of DAGs for which this problem can be resolved in polynomial time, and we provide an efficient planar drawing algorithm for those groups.

The proliferation of configurable modern system architectures demands a focus on streamlining their configuration, thereby enhancing overall development cycle agility. To address this, we introduce a novel approach that automates the configuration process by leveraging statistical methods to analyze historical data and infer optimal settings. Specifically, we utilize a hybrid algorithm combining Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with the Beta-Beta-Binomial model. This algorithm iteratively refines its strategy by learning from past successes and failures to identify the most effective configuration. We validated this method against the Random and Best-of-N baselines using data from the Apache Software Foundation's Incubator Project Dashboard. Results indicate that this approach outperforms the random baseline and the Best-of-N baseline in 95% of system metrics, offering a robust solution for automating configuration in complex environments.

Beam breakup instability represents a critical challenge in the development of high-gradient, high-field superconducting radio frequency (RF) cavities for next-generation particle accelerators, ultimately restricting maximum beam current. To address this, researchers have proposed employing detuned sidebands within the cavity fundamental mode to reduce the breakdown effect. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the BBU phenomenon in both linear and nonlinear regimes when utilizing such sidebands. A novel linear theory is developed to determine the corresponding growth rates and eigen-bunch shapes, while an innovative computational algorithm is introduced to trace bunch evolution over extended durations, thereby facilitating a direct comparison between theoretical predictions and experimental outcomes. Observations from the Superconducting Linear Test Stand (SLTS) at Fermilab are utilized to validate the proposed models. Results indicate that a significant reduction in the BBU phenomenon occurs in the nonlinear regime relative to linear forecasts, with the derived bunch shapes aligning closely with measured data. Furthermore, the analysis demonstrates that a factor of ten improvement in BBU performance is achievable in the nonlinear regime compared to baseline operations without detuning.

Three-dimensional projection scintillator trackers are emerging as a vital technology for upcoming neutrino oscillation experiments, offering a compact footprint with high granularity, rapid scalability, and straightforward readout mechanisms. This study introduces a novel, cost-effective readout architecture for these 3D scintillator projection trackers, utilizing optical fibers coupled to scintillator elements to transmit light to photodiodes. This optical fiber network arranges light collection in a two-dimensional matrix, significantly reducing the quantity of electronic channels required. The feasibility of this design was demonstrated through a prototype module featuring a 4 × 4 grid of 4 × 4 × 1 mm³ scintillator cells connected to a photodiode array via optical fibers. This study examines the sticking forces between two chondritic grains, each with a radius of 100 $\mu$m, under conditions of surface water ice. Using a continuum model, we analyze how sticking forces vary with temperature and water ice thickness. Our findings indicate that at 20 K, the force peaks at approximately 1.5 N when the ice layer reaches 0.01 $\mu$m thick. Conversely, at 100 K, the maximum force is about 0.1 N, occurring at an ice thickness of 0.1 $\mu$m. Additionally, we evaluated the impact of a viscous substrate on these forces and found that for a 100 $\mu$m grain, a substrate viscosity of 10 Pa s results in a force roughly 100 times greater than that of a substrate with 1000 Pa s viscosity. These results have significant implications for understanding the transition from sticking to bouncing behavior observed in recent research.

Local Fisher Discriminant Analysis (LFDA) serves as a widely adopted technique for semi-supervised dimensionality reduction. This study introduces semi-supervised LFDA kernels (SSL-FDA-K), which construct affinity matrices to flexibly manage diverse non-linear data structures. These FDA-K kernels are applied to generate feature representations for a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), enabling effective classification of point cloud data. Our proposed methodology, known as FDA-K-PointNet, integrates these components to form a cohesive pipeline. Experiments conducted on five benchmark datasets demonstrate that this approach not only achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods but also generalizes effectively to novel viewpoints.

Imitation learning stands as a powerful paradigm for robot skill acquisition, enabling the mastery of complex behaviors by learning directly from demonstrations. Among various techniques, movement primitives are particularly prominent for their ability to generalize across different task scenarios. This study introduces a novel approach grounded in extended kernelized movement primitives, which enhances the robustness of acquired skills against disturbances and disruptions during execution. Specifically, three distinct kernel functions are employed to map task-space trajectories into a high-dimensional latent space. Learning occurs by aligning latent trajectories of robot arms with those of target tasks, ensuring that the resulting behaviors accurately reflect the task's geometry. Crucially, extending kernelization to latent space facilitates the decoupling of task-level instructions from robot-specific configuration details. This decoupling ensures that tasks transfer reliably to various workspaces, while allowing adaptation to specific manipulators simply by relearning the latent trajectory in the task's latent representation. To validate these concepts, the authors present simulation studies and physical experiments involving a dual-arm robot tasked with manipulating an object alongside a single-arm robot performing point-to-point movements.

We investigate the interplay of Rashba spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman field in a two-dimensional BCS superconductor, deriving the corresponding gap equation and its solutions across various parameter regimes. Our analysis reveals that spin-orbit coupling induces a re-entrant behavior where superconducting stability is restored at higher Zeeman strengths after an initial suppression. Furthermore, we demonstrate that spin-orbit coupling generates two distinct types of triplet pairing, characterized by different spin textures and emerging at separate points in the parameter space. We further analyze the influence of these spin-orbit effects on the pairing gap magnitude and the critical density required for the transition between singlet and triplet superconducting phases.

We present a refined framework for analyzing polymer brushes on curved surfaces, advancing the classical mean-field theory by introducing an end exclusion zone around each tethering point where other chain ends are prohibited from entering. On a sphere of radius $R$, this mechanism generates a size disparity between chains anchored at the poles versus those at the equator; specifically, for fixed $R$ and large degrees of polymerization $N$, equatorial chains scale as $N^{1+\nu}$ times larger than polar ones (with $\nu \approx 0.75$ for good solvents), a difference that amplifies as $N$ increases. This effect persists on other curved geometries, such as cylinders, and remains significant even when $R$ is large relative to the monomer size $a$, provided the degree of polymerization is sufficiently high.

Let $G=(V,E)$ denote a connected graph with vertex set $V$ and edge set $E$. A subset $W \subseteq V$ is termed a *resolving set* if the distances from every vertex in $G$ to the elements of $W$ uniquely identify that vertex; the smallest possible size of such a set defines the graph's *metric dimension*. This study introduces several new concepts related to metric dimension, specifically proving that a graph $G$ possesses a resolving set $W$ consisting of exactly $k$ vertices if and only if the $k$-dimensional metric basis of $G$ comprises all $k$! distinct permutations of the vector $d(x,W)$, where $x \in G$ and $d(x,W)$ represents the distance vector. Furthermore, we derive a novel closed-form formula for computing the $k$-dimensional metric basis. Finally, the application of these findings is demonstrated through the analysis of the line graphs of stars and complete graphs.

We address a broad class of combinatorial optimization problems where agents possess restricted feasible sets and valuations, seeking an outcome that maximizes total social welfare. We propose a deterministic protocol called serial dictatorship, applicable to each problem instance by ordering agents and allocating resources sequentially. Although serial dictatorship is straightforward, its efficacy varies; to quantify this, we evaluate its expected performance by averaging over all $n!$ possible agent orderings. Our analysis demonstrates that, for a wide range of settings, this expected social welfare is within a factor of $O(\sqrt{n})$ of the optimal. Furthermore, we evaluate alternative mechanisms, including randomized algorithms, and find that no approach can surpass an approximation ratio of $\Omega(n^{1/2- \epsilon})$ for any $\epsilon > 0$, assuming the optimal social welfare is at least $\Omega(n^{1/2+\epsilon})$.

We report the discovery of a wide separation binary asteroid, designated 2004 BL66, with a primary diameter of 1.1 km, a primary-to-secondary diameter ratio of 1:0.15, and an orbital period of 11.1 days. This object was identified through photometric follow-up of the Catalina Real-time Transient Survey (CRTS) discovery, which initially flagged 2004 BL66 as an anomalous long-duration asteroid event likely caused by mutual eclipses. The findings provide valuable insights into binary formation mechanisms and internal structure, given the rarity of such widely separated binaries that serve as key tracers for stable binary evolution and the mass estimation of minor planets.

This paper introduces several variations of Leibniz rules specifically formulated for Riemann-Liouville variable-order integral operators, along with corresponding fractional derivative rules. A foundational result establishes the four distinct types of product rules—left and right applied to integrals and derivatives respectively.
