Current passive satellite retrieval techniques struggle with highly developed convective clouds, specifically regarding optical thickness and effective particle size assessments. This study proposes a novel 3D radiative transfer model designed to simulate the spectral characteristics of such structures. The proposed approach treats the vertical optical thickness and effective 3D particle radius within distinct convective layers as independent variables. By leveraging spectral data from the Clouds and Earth's Radiant Energy System (CREDS) instrument aboard the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES-R), the method employs an inversion technique to derive the 3D optical thickness and particle size for each individual layer. Validation against Cloud-Cockpit Instrumentation (C-CI) measurements from the Kwajalein Atoll in the Marshall Islands demonstrates strong alignment between simulated and observed spectral data, with the model successfully reconstructing the multi-layered optical thickness and particle size profiles derived from C-CI. The resulting 3D optical thickness and particle size estimates match the original C-CI input data with a root-mean-square deviation of 12.5% and 8.2%, respectively. The study concludes that this technique offers a viable pathway for generating highly accurate 3D optical thickness and particle size assessments for convective systems using GOES-R spectral data.

This study examines how a laser pulse with positive chirp propagates through plasma, utilizing the fully relativistic, nonlinear two-fluid model to simulate the process. The analysis reveals that chirping the pulse significantly influences the threshold plasma density needed for transmission; specifically, a laser pulse featuring positive chirp requires a higher threshold density compared to an unchirped or negatively chirped pulse. Furthermore, the model demonstrates that positive chirp enhances the interaction between the laser and plasma, resulting in the generation of higher-energy electrons and ions. The simulation also indicates that the peak intensity of the pulse increases as the magnitude of the chirp becomes larger. Finally, the model confirms that the plasma density directly impacts chirp effectiveness, with greater enhancement in electron and ion energy observed when the chirp operates at lower densities.

The first billion years of a planet's life are critical for its evolution, during which the young star's intense X-ray and ultraviolet (XUV) radiation significantly drives atmospheric escape and drives the loss of primordial atmospheres. While the Sun's XUV history is relatively well documented, data for other stars remains sparse. This study utilizes the extensive Chandra X-ray Observatory archive to reconstruct the XUV evolution of five young G-type stars: HD 31617, HD 5182, HD 52265, and two of the Sun's analogs. The analysis reveals that these stars exhibit a complex evolutionary trajectory characterized by a gradual decline in XUV emission over their initial 100 million years, contrasting with the "XUV flare" seen in younger systems. Consequently, any planets orbiting these stars would have experienced substantial atmospheric stripping early in their history.

Using first-principles calculations, we investigated the structural and electronic characteristics of C and N impurities substituting into TiO$_2$ to explore their potential for spin filtering. Our findings indicate that isolated C and N atoms in substitutional sites within TiO$_2$ exhibit magnetic properties, whereas a C-C or N-N pair displays antiferromagnetic coupling. Furthermore, a CN pair connected by a single bond demonstrates robust magnetism, exhibiting a ground state with an anomalous CN configuration distinct from those observed in gas phase or other crystal lattices. Finally, we examined various CN alignments and discovered that the CN configuration oriented perpendicular to the rutgle c-axis generates a transmission current with 100\% spin polarization.

This study examines forward proton tagging as a discriminant for distinguishing t-channel from s-channel top-quark pair ($t\bar{t}$) production, based on matrix element techniques. In this approach, the presence of scattered protons in the tag allows for the reconstruction of the collision center-of-mass energy, denoted as $\hat{s}$. Results indicate that the transverse momenta of the top quarks within these two production categories exhibit distinct distributions, enabling discrimination between them. Furthermore, analysis of $\hat{s}$ distributions reveals that top quarks generated via the s-channel predominantly cluster around $\hat{s} \simeq m_{t\bar{t}}^2/m_t$, whereas those from the t-channel display a uniform distribution. Utilizing these characteristics, the study establishes a selection criterion for s-channel events defined by $|\hat{s} - m_{t\bar{t}}^2/m_t| < 100~\text{GeV}$. This selection achieves a signal purity of 90\% and retains 40\% signal efficiency. Additionally, the work demonstrates that this method remains viable even when proton tagging is combined with jet charge measurements.

X-ray observations of the hot, X-ray emitting gas in galaxy clusters allow for the direct measurement of non-thermal pressure support, which arises from the random motions of gas parcels. This phenomenon is typically quantified by calculating the turbulent Mach number, defined as the ratio of turbulent velocity to the local sound speed. In this study, we determine non-thermal support values for 14 relaxed galaxy clusters by analyzing the velocity dispersion of gas tracers across multiple spatial scales. Our findings indicate that non-thermal support is spatially uniform, with a mean turbulent Mach number of 0.11 and a maximum of 0.17. We further demonstrate that this level of turbulence is insufficient to overcome gravitational cooling, suggesting that non-thermal support alone cannot explain the observed population of cool cores. Additionally, our results imply that turbulence cannot be the primary mechanism driving large-scale mixing in galaxy clusters.

This work introduces a new framework for the design and analysis of graph states and their associated measurement-based quantum computations utilizing qudits. We demonstrate that constructing a target graph state composed of higher-dimensional charges (qudits) can be achieved through local partitioning of the system, applying qubit-only construction techniques within each local subspace. Furthermore, we derive fundamental relations linking the parameters of the target qudit graph state to those of the constituent qubit states. Specifically, we show that the target can be formed by aggregating multiple qubit graph states per locality, with their parameters related via novel formulas we introduce: the locality expansion formula and the planar cutting formula. In addition, we propose a specific class of qudit graph states characterized by the superposition of identical graph states across all loci, and we derive rules for determining their parameters based on the superposed components. Finally, we establish a direct correspondence between computational steps for qudits and their qubit counterparts, proving that a qudit gate or single-site Z-basis measurement can be decomposed into a sequence of specific qubit operations tailored to the system's dimension.

High-intensity laser-solid interactions have emerged as a promising avenue for generating high-quality positrons, potentially enabling the creation of positron beams with notable polarization. In this study, we present a two-dimensional (2D) model designed to simulate positron spin dynamics arising from these interactions. Our approach integrates a 2D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation framework with the Dirac equation solved via the multigrid method on a fixed grid. By employing a hybridization of the Euler and Leapfrog integration schemes, our model achieves a balance between computational efficiency and numerical accuracy. Simulation outcomes indicate that positron spin polarization arises from the interplay of the laser's electromagnetic field, the positron's own electromagnetic field, and the target's electromagnetic field. Specifically, the degree of spin polarization is influenced by the relative phase of the laser pulse, the positron density, and the target's surface orientation. Furthermore, our results demonstrate that the inclusion of the positron field significantly enhances the final polarization level compared to scenarios where the positron field is neglected.

This study introduces an integrated CMOS temperature sensor designed to support thermal-aware dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS). By integrating this sensor into systems that adjust operating points based on temperature, we can infer the necessary voltage and frequency levels through a lookup table, eliminating the need for direct frequency counters or cycle calculations typically required for DVFS. Instead of relying on time-based measurements, the sensor utilizes temperature-dependent propagation delays to track clock cycles. Furthermore, the design incorporates an energy-efficient mechanism that reduces the sensor's operating frequency and voltage in response to rising temperatures. Experimental results demonstrate a 94% reduction in power consumption compared to standard sensor configurations and confirm accurate cycle counting with an error margin of less than 1%.

The origin of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) remains one of the most pressing mysteries in astrophysics. A primary theory posits that UHECRs are generated by protons accelerated to extreme energies within the energetic environments surrounding active galactic nuclei (AGN). This study presents a novel methodology for identifying potential neutrino signatures associated with such hadron-dominated AGN. We analyze the neutrino spectra produced by protons accelerated in the immediate vicinity of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) within AGN, utilizing the multiwavelength spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of AGN from the Fermi-LAT gamma-ray catalog and the NuSTAR X-ray catalog. Our analysis reveals that approximately 1000 AGN are capable of generating the ultra-high-energy neutrinos detected by the IceCube observatory. Furthermore, we identify roughly 100 "neutrino-emitting" AGN candidates that exhibit strong, distinct neutrino emission. These candidates are proposed as prime sites for investigating the origins of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays.

The rheology of complex liquids is highly sensitive to interfacial roughness, a factor that generates diverse frictional regimes and yields valuable insights into microscopic dynamics. This study details the frictional behavior of a model complex liquid across a broad spectrum of rough surfaces, revealing three distinct regimes. For the first time, the study demonstrates that these regimes are defined by surface roughness metrics and roughness scale relative to the liquid's correlation length. Specifically, Regime I occurs on surfaces where roughness scales are smaller than the correlation length, causing the liquid to perceive the surface as intrinsically smooth; here, roughness metrics dictate friction levels. Regime II emerges on surfaces with roughness scales comparable to the correlation length, where the liquid is sensitive to both roughness magnitude and scale, and is associated with dynamic freezing of the liquid's microstructure. Regime III occurs on surfaces where roughness scales exceed the correlation length, resulting in friction independent of roughness scale but dependent on the magnitude of roughness metrics, analogous to the averaging of white noise. Finally, the study evaluates the implications of these findings for optimizing the wettability of complex liquids.

In ISIC challenge 2019, 170 dermoscopic images of melanoma were provided for diagnosis assistance. This study examines an elastic membrane within a rotating system, separating two fluids with differing densities and viscosities, to investigate how centrifugal forces trigger fingering instability driven by rotation. Analyzing the system under both linear and highly nonlinear regimes, we determine the conditions required for the development of finger-like deformations. Our analysis of the linear regime allows us to establish a clear criterion for the onset of instability, which we validate against numerical simulations across a broad spectrum of parameters. Furthermore, we explore the complex nonlinear dynamics, specifically focusing on the growth of fingers and the subsequent formation of closed loops.

This study examines the free expansion of a fluid within an isolated system, initially in a state away from equilibrium across a membrane separating two chambers of unequal volumes. Upon puncturing the membrane, the fluid eventually reaches a new steady state. We analyze this process by comparing two metrics for final steady states: (i) the minimum time required to reach said state starting from the initial condition, and (ii) the minimum dissipation needed given a fixed duration. Our findings indicate that, regardless of whether the transition prioritizes minimum duration or minimum dissipation, the fluid invariably moves from a state exhibiting negative microwork to one exhibiting positive microwork. Conversely, whether the expansion proceeds under minimum time control (irrespective of total dissipation) or minimum dissipation control (irrespective of total duration), the final states are never arbitrarily distant from the initial state in terms of thermodynamic metric distance.

We report the results of a 100-day survey targeting ethynyl benzene ($C_6H_5C\equiv CH$, hereafter $e$-$C_7H_8$) using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA). The survey covered a $10'' \times 10''$ area centered on the LMC N49 nebula with an angular resolution of $4'' \times 4''$ and a $3\sigma$ sensitivity corresponding to a $10'' \times 10''$ integration time. No $e$-$C_7H_8$ emission was detected, establishing an upper limit for a $3\sigma$ flux density of $0.10$ Jy at the $J=1_{0,0} \rightarrow 0_{0,0}$ transition ($\sim 552.9$ GHz). This limit translates to a column density ceiling of $1.6 \times 10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$ ($3\sigma$) and $5.0 \times 10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$ ($90\%$ confidence). Consequently, future detections will require either higher sensitivity, larger beam-averaged areas, or observations of sources with column densities exceeding $10^{15}$ cm$^{-2}$.

Attention mechanisms have become integral to various natural language processing tasks, including neural machine translation (NMT). In NMT attention, the distribution used to generate each target token depends not only on the source context but also on the history of previously generated target words. This paper introduces a new attention mechanism specifically designed for NMT that incorporates structural knowledge regarding the dependency between these historical generations. By modeling this dependency through a probability distribution over potential regions of interest among past generated words, the approach effectively improves machine translation performance.

The field of translational medicine, which focuses on converting scientific discoveries into tangible improvements in health, relies heavily on the integration of data from multiple sources. Consequently, advanced analytics and machine learning have become essential for discovering patterns within this diverse information. This review examines the application of machine learning techniques in medical analytics, with a specific emphasis on methods designed to handle integrated datasets. Various strategies for effectively combining data are explored, alongside models capable of extracting insights and generating predictions. Finally, significant real-world examples of successful data integration in medicine are presented, demonstrating how these approaches facilitate the translation of discoveries into practical health benefits.

This study investigates a coherent dissipative dark fluid framework combining an Aria-Kassamli (AK) fluid with Hubble dissipation and power-law heating. We establish the conservation laws for this model and analyze its phase space structure. Our analysis reveals that the fluid's equation of state parameter, $w_{\rm eff}$, oscillates between $-1$ and $1$, avoiding the phantom divide. By solving the system's governing equations, we identify three distinct cosmological scenarios: (i) a universe dominated by AK fluid that decelerates throughout its evolution, (ii) an AK fluid-dominated era transitioning to dark energy domination, resulting in deceleration followed by acceleration, and (iii) a scenario yielding an oscillating expansion rate where the AK fluid drives both deceleration and acceleration phases. Furthermore, we derive the thermodynamic properties of the fluid, demonstrating that its entropy production adheres to the second law of thermodynamics. Finally, we construct the complete dynamical system, determining all critical points and evaluating their cosmological and physical implications.

Curiosity is fundamental to fostering creativity and a passion for learning within educational environments. Yet, it remains unclear how specific classroom practices cultivate this trait. This study investigates the role of curiosity in the learning process and examines its connection to intrinsic motivation. The research posits that curiosity functions as a self-regulated learning mechanism, driven by an individual's desire to resolve knowledge gaps. Furthermore, the paper highlights the distinction between two forms: state curiosity, which is transient, and trait curiosity, which is enduring. Drawing on these concepts, the authors outline a theoretical framework linking classroom activities to state trait curiosity and subsequent learning outcomes. Finally, the paper proposes a research agenda designed to empirically test this framework.

Gaussian processes serve as a versatile tool for modeling stochastic functions across various settings, including undirected graphs. This paper introduces GpGraph, a user-friendly Python toolkit designed to simplify working with Gaussian processes on the graph domain. The package supports regression and classification tasks, covering both Markov and non-Markovian frameworks, and is fully compatible with stochastic differential equation (SDE) solvers found in the DifferentialEquations.jl ecosystem on Julia. Additionally, GpGraph provides robust MCMC and variational inference mechanisms, enabling efficient model training and evaluation for practitioners.

Monitoring urban road networks is essential for enhancing transportation efficiency and mitigating congestion. Nevertheless, existing congestion monitoring methods suffer from significant drawbacks, including high costs, limited coverage, and data sparsity. This study introduces a novel concept for sensing urban road networks known as URS, which leverages the interactions between connected vehicles and self-driving trucks carrying unpressurized cargo tanks. Given that these vehicles are prevalent in the transport of industrial chemicals and fuels, they offer an ideal medium for sensing based on their ubiquity. The URS framework relies on the interaction between CIOs (Connected Intelligent Vehicles) and self-driving trucks carrying unpressurized cargo tanks. This paper investigates the decay of $J/\psi$ into light sterile neutrinos, which subsequently decay into lepton-electron pairs via mixing with active neutrinos. We establish a lower bound on the branching ratio for $J/\psi \to \text{invisible}$ at $> 0.14\%$, exceeding prior constraints by an order of magnitude. This enhancement is achieved by leveraging the initial and final state radiation of leptons within the $e^+e^- \to J/\psi + X$ process to significantly enhance the sensitivity of searches for invisible decays. Additionally, we constrain the partial width for $J/\psi \to s \bar{s} s s$ utilizing the same dataset, improving previous limits by a factor of 100. These results constrain the mass of light sterile neutrinos to exceed 4.6 GeV, assuming a total width less than $10^{-5}$ eV.

Second derivative general linear methods (SGLMs) have been employed to approximate solutions of non-stiff ordinary differential equations (ODEs) systems. This paper introduces a class of second derivative implicit Runge-Kutta methods (IRK) coupled with the inverse matrix technique for solving systems where the Jacobian matrix is non-invertible. A convergence theorem is established for these proposed methods, and numerical experiments are conducted to evaluate their performance.

This paper introduces Multivariate Functional Singular Spectrum Analysis (MFSSA), a tool designed to analyze multivariate functional time series signals. While standard Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) has been extended to functional domains, MFSSA distinguishes itself by integrating dimension reduction techniques, specifically canonical correlation analysis (CCA), to uncover complex dependencies among multiple functional variables. By decomposing signals into various components, this approach enables the visualization of component-wise covariances and facilitates the detection of structural breaks. To demonstrate its efficacy, we apply MFSSA to analyze daily closing prices of the S&P 500 index and the CDS sub-indices for US, Europe, and Asia, revealing distinct structural shifts in both individual country trajectories and their inter-country relationships.

Modern automated essay scoring (AES) systems have become increasingly popular, with top-tier models achieving performance comparable to human raters. AES research has expanded significantly, covering a wide range of techniques. However, existing works often lack shared terminology, leading to confusion regarding the specific attributes that drive the success of top AES models. This paper provides a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art AES systems, organizing them into three primary categories: end-to-end scoring models, multi-task learning approaches, and pairwise ranking systems. Furthermore, the authors examine critical success factors such as input data, text evaluation metrics, and scoring functions. Finally, key resources for AES research—including public datasets, scoring platforms, and essential tools—are highlighted.

This study addresses the problem of determining constants $\alpha$ and $\beta$ such that ${\bf P}(\sum_{i=1}^n X_i \geq 0) = n^{-\alpha} (\ln n)^{\beta} + o(n^{-\alpha} (\ln n)^{\beta})$ holds for i.i.d. real random variables with mean zero and symmetric, power-law decaying ($\alpha \in (0,2)$) stable distributions. We establish these parameters for the case where $\alpha \neq 1/2$, covering cases with or without logarithmic corrections. Conversely, when $\alpha=1/2$, we provide a counterexample demonstrating that the proposed asymptotic form can fail.

This study examines the plasma discharge characteristics of a helicon source, with a specific focus on the transition to the skin mode of discharge. The paper details the experimental setup, the measurement protocols, and the diagnostic tools utilized. The results indicate that the transition to the skin mode occurs at a peak peak-to-peak radiofrequency (rf) voltage of 1.5 kV, a level significantly lower than the 3.5 kV typically required for this transition in standard helicon sources. This low-voltage transition facilitates the operation of high-density plasma at reduced rf power levels. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that the transition to the skin mode can be triggered by manipulating the rf power phase relative to the peak electron cyclotron resonance frequency, rather than solely relying on increasing voltage and density.

Microbial pesticides represent a promising avenue for controlling plant diseases, offering a sustainable alternative to conventional chemical agents. Although the spectrum of available microbial pesticides continues to expand, the development of new options often lags behind the rate at which pathogens develop resistance to existing chemicals. A primary benefit of these microbial agents lies in their target specificity, which helps preserve beneficial microorganisms within the agricultural ecosystem. Furthermore, leveraging the genetic diversity inherent in natural microbial populations enables the sustained efficacy of these treatments. This study introduces a novel computational framework designed to analyze population dynamics within microbial systems. By utilizing the stochastic generalized Lotka-Volterra framework, the proposed method capitalizes on the flexibility of Bayesian inference methods, specifically Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling, to analyze complex population interactions. The resulting methodology facilitates a deeper understanding of these systems by facilitating the estimation of unknown model parameters and facilitating the rigorous evaluation of competing theoretical models. The robustness and advantages of this new framework are demonstrated through its application to a dataset concerning *Bacillus thuringiensis* (*Bt*) dynamics infecting *Plutella xylostella* (the diamondback moth).

Automatic cancer diagnosis relies heavily on identifying cancer cells, yet the need for large, expert-annotated datasets poses a significant challenge to developing nucleus segmentation models. This scarcity is particularly acute in cancer care, where obtaining numerous labeled images is difficult. To address this, this paper introduces a novel data augmentation strategy that expands training datasets by synthesizing nuclei from unlabeled images. The approach employs a two-stage framework: it first trains a deep learning model to detect cell locations and then uses those detections to extract and insert nuclei into new images. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated across three distinct datasets, including one containing only unlabeled images. Results indicate that the proposed approach achieves a Dice Coefficient of 0.890, surpassing state-of-the-art models that depend on extensive annotated data.

Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field. This study establishes a criterion determining when two irreducible admissible generic representations of $GL_n(F)$ are isomorphic. The criterion relies on the equality of their $L$-parameters and the specific isomorphism type of the underlying $W$-parameter for $W_F$, the Weil group of $F$. These findings yield new insights into the local Langlands correspondence for $GL_n$ over such fields.

Xiong and Liu previously established that for any graph $G$ with $n \geq 3$ vertices, its $n$-th iterated line graph $L^n(G)$ always possesses a spanning path. In this paper, we go further by demonstrating that $L^n(G)$ necessarily contains a Hamilton path, provided the original graph $G$ is simple, connected, and has a minimum degree of at least 2, under the condition $n \geq k+1$ where $k$ represents the smallest integer for which $L^k(G)$ becomes Hamiltonian. Furthermore, we derive an upper bound for $k$.

Pyroptosis represents a highly conserved, regulated form of inflammatory cell death triggered by intracellular pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) and danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs). This process is intrinsically linked to the activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, which facilitates the cleavage of gasdermin D (GSDMD) and pro-IL-1β, resulting in cell lation and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-1β. Consequently, pyroptosis serves as a critical host defense mechanism against microbial infections and is also implicated in various inflammatory diseases. Pharmacological agents targeting pyroptosis hold significant potential for treating conditions like atherosclerosis, rheumatoid arthritis, and sepsis. In this review, we examine the molecular architecture of the NLRP3 inflammasome, the structural features of GSDMD, and the regulatory networks surrounding their activation. Furthermore, we explore the therapeutic applications of non-antibiotic-derived pyroptosis inhibitors.

In reinforcement learning, exogenous state variables and rewards can either hinder performance or enhance it. While the adverse effects of such stochasticity have been extensively examined, this work investigates the mechanism by which favorable exogenous states accelerate learning. We demonstrate that the variance introduced by these stochastic elements creates interference among value estimates, a phenomenon that decays exponentially with the dimensionality of the state space. Drawing on this insight, we introduce a dimensionality-adjusted learning rate strategy designed to specifically mitigate this variance. Our experimental results indicate that this approach significantly accelerates learning in both linear and nonlinear settings compared to conventional constant learning rates, particularly as space dimensions increase.

Smart contracts represent a key innovation in blockchain technology, automating actions and decisions through rule-based logic. However, current approaches often rely on implicit assumptions and ad-hoc methods to determine when these conditions are met, which can introduce errors and security risks. This paper introduces a formal framework utilizing temporal logic to specify both decision-making rules and their triggering events for smart contracts. We developed an implementation of this formal system in Solidity, the language used for Ethereum-based contracts. Our approach supports the automatic generation of code snippets that handle logic related to contract activation, as well as the synthesis of invariants essential for formal verification. Testing with multiple real-world contracts demonstrates that our solution successfully produces working implementations and establishes robust security invariants.

Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNN) have recently emerged as a powerful tool for solving complex problems in computer science and engineering. In a GCNN, convolution layers serve as the core component, yet their graph-based implementation has been unclear, leading to numerous inconsistent definitions. This study introduces a graph-based image fusion framework utilizing Image Fusion (IG) as a central element. Our approach models the relationship between input images and the output image through a mapping function, which is optimized by a loss function designed to maximize image quality metrics. Specifically, we derive the exact formulation for the graph convolution layer by treating the fusion process as a graph signal processing task. Our results indicate that existing realizations of these layers often contain flaws, whereas the proposed method offers a robust solution. Experimental comparisons demonstrate that our framework outperforms current state-of-the-art image fusion methods.

We examine the existence of self-gravitating scalar solitons within Einstein-Yelets-Maxwell theory, where both the scalar potential and the holonomy of associated connections must be required to have trivial values. Discoveries indicate that the necessity for this trivial holonomy ensures the existence of these solitons, acting as a mechanism to prevent the formation of event horizons. Furthermore, we find that imposing trivial holonomy forces a strict inverse square law behavior on these objects at large distances, a constraint that can be relaxed by introducing a non-minimal coupling between the scalar field and the Ricci scalar.

We demonstrate that $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theories featuring the $${\mathfrak{so}(4N}}$$ Lie algebra possess a set of non-invertible symmetries. These are identified by computing the complete collection of topological defect lines and surface defects within the corresponding supersymmetric quantum mechanics model that describes the matter sector. By synthesizing these defect data, we construct an intricate defect algebra and determine its Grothendieck group, which serves as a symmetry group containing the identified defect elements. As a supplementary finding, we establish a correspondence between these defect data and those found in the superconformal quantum mechanics associated with the ${\mathfrak{p}(4N}}$$ algebra.

Ultrasound elastography maps internal tissue mechanical properties by analyzing deformation responses to external forces, offering a non-invasive method for tissue characterization. A critical factor influencing elastography quality is spatial resolution, which Virtual Source Synthetic Aperture (VSSA) enhances by synthesizing a larger effective aperture. However, VSSA introduces a focal zone that is both shallow and narrow, creating a trade-off. This study introduces an advanced imaging strategy combining VSSA with focused techniques to resolve that limitation. The proposed approach captures data using the VSSA method at various fixed, shallow focal positions, subsequently reconstructing the image via summation. Validation was performed on ex vivo porcine liver specimens using a linear array probe operating at 5.5 MHz. Results indicate that this new method achieves spatial resolution comparable to standard SA imaging but offers superior contrast ratio and a broader region of high quality.

"Proving systems function as meta-interpretations of algorithms, where the theorems they prove correspond to the logical outcomes guaranteed by the algorithm. This paper introduces a specific imperative algorithm designed to generate all provable statements within a certain class of proofs belonging to the Colecta logic proof system. By design, this algorithm establishes a direct, constructive link between imperative computing and formal proof theory. Furthermore, it demonstrates that high-level algorithms can be utilized to meta-interpret constructive proofs, thereby creating a functional bridge where executing the algorithm not only generates a proof but also embodies its constructive embodiment."

The tuple $(\mathbf{P}_1, \dots, \mathbf{P}_k)$ defines a $k$-colored Boolean poset if there exists a Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ whose subgraph induced by all $0$-values is isomorphic to $\mathbf{P}_1$ and the subgraph induced by all $1$-values can be partitioned into $k-1$ induced subgraphs isomorphic to $\mathbf{P}_2, \dots, \mathbf{P}_k$, respectively. We examine the $k$-means clustering problem within the dynamic streaming model, where points either enter or leave the stream. By approximating cluster centers using random samplings based on point dynamics, we present an $\tilde O(k/\epsilon^2)$-space algorithm for the distinct element model. This algorithm achieves a factor of $1+\epsilon$ approximation regarding the optimal clustering cost, covering both the standard and strengthened objective functions. Furthermore, by applying this result to the Strong Objective in the turn model specifically (where points must revisit), we derive a $(1+\delta)$ factor approximation for some suitable $\delta > 0$.

This study addresses the challenge of executing discrete stochastic pursuit-evasion games (PEGs) on large, highly symmetric graphs when both the pursuit and evasion entities operate with limited communication bandwidth. To achieve this, we propose a hierarchical framework. The core of our approach involves solving an equivalent, more compact PEG defined on a graph hierarchy, which allows for reduced data transmission. Subsequently, the system executes the corresponding local game at each symmetric subgraph component independently. We evaluate this method on the "Game of Cops and Robbers" played on a Torus graph. Results indicate that this hierarchical strategy reduces communication requirements by several orders of magnitude compared to traditional methods.

Inspired by the well-known i.i.d. property, we introduce the concept of cyclic independence for random variables tied to n-tuples that satisfy specific $n$-cycle conditions. Drawing on these definitions and associated lemmas, we derive the limit theorem for cyclic sums involving power functions.

Deep learning techniques have demonstrated significant efficacy in denoising low-dose CT (LDCT) images. CycleGAN architectures have been employed to generate smooth standard-dose (SDCT) images from LDCT image domains; however, utilizing two separate generators—one for each direction—introduces a risk of cycle inconsistencies. To address this, we introduce a novel cycLoCT framework that utilizes a single switchable generator instead of dual generators. By imposing hard constraints to prevent the model from learning domain-specific features, this design ensures cycle consistency. Experiments indicate that cycLoCT outperforms cycGAN methods in terms of denoising efficacy and demonstrates superior cycle consistency, characterized by lower cycle loss values and higher structural similarity metrics.

Pre-training on a vast corpus of unstructured conversations has emerged as a promising approach to enhancing supervised dialog understanding. Current methods typically rely on RNN-based architectures, which often yield suboptimal performance. This paper introduces TreeCoT, a conversational CoT (Conditional on Topic) model that utilizes a tree-structured pre-training framework. We first introduce the concept of the "topic tree," which captures the hierarchical progression of topics within a dialogue. Building on this, we present two novel loss functions: one for predicting the topic tree structure given the full dialogue history and another for generating detailed topic nodes that summarize partial sub-dialogues. Experiments conducted on the MultiWOZ dataset demonstrate that TreeCoT achieves a State-of-the-Art (SOTA) Slot Filling accuracy of 83.4% and an Intent Classification accuracy of 94.1%.

This study explores the geometric characteristics of conformal Ricci-Yamabe solitons within conformally related warped product manifolds. It categorizes these solitons as expanding, steady, or shrinking based on the behavior of the underlying warped product structure—specifically linking their classification to whether the structure is contracting, stable, or shrinking.

Utilizing the Generator Mean Field (GMF) framework, we examine the spatial structure of these states and the underlying mechanisms driving their rotational dynamics. We analyze the forward gauge radiation that occurs in lepton collisions at energies exceeding several TeV. By integrating this gauge radiation with the QCD parton distribution functions of protons, we establish a novel colliding-photon–proton framework applicable to facilities like the Future Circular Collider. Our findings demonstrate that, in the extreme forward region where photon virtualities remain low, the standard (unstructured) QCD photon PDFs are significantly enhanced by forward radiation. This effect is particularly pronounced for $W^\pm$ and $Z$ bosons, yielding parton luminosity increases of up to $10^5$ for $\gamma W^\pm$ and $10^4$ for $\gamma\gamma$ interactions. Consequently, such radiation enables the Future Circular Collider to perform precision measurements of $\gamma Z\gamma$-fusion processes, including those involving $W^\pm$ pair production via $\gamma\gamma$ fusion, as well as access to the extremely rare $\gamma W^\pm$-fusion channel for $t\bar{\gamma}$ (top quark) pair creation. Furthermore, this mechanism permits the first direct probe of $\gamma\gamma$-box diagrams to test lepton universality in the third generation, specifically examining the $\tau$ lepton. In multi-task reinforcement learning, agents typically improve by training on multiple related tasks while relying on knowledge gained from one to enhance their interaction with another. However, this paper questions the assumption that all tasks are beneficial, arguing that some can degrade overall performance. To address this, we propose a new framework for adaptive task selection in a fully autonomous setting, where a system autonomously decides which tasks to execute. Our approach employs a novel meta-reward function that evaluates task selection decisions based on both individual task outcomes and the impact of those tasks on others. Experiments in both a grid-world environment and a MuJoCo-based robot simulation demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

In this paper, we obtain Li-Yau type gradient estimates, specifically Souplet-Zhang generalizations, for the equation $\Delta_{\mathcal{M}} u = \lambda u - u^p$ defined on complete, noncompact $n$-dimensional cones $\mathcal{M}$. These cones possess a metric $g = dt^2 + t^2 h$, where $(C_n, h)$ represents a complete cone-manifold with nonnegative sectional curvature. Our findings yield concrete bounds on the blow-up profile and its gradient for solutions to the equation $\Delta_{\mathcal{M}} u = \lambda u - u^p$ on such spaces.

These findings fundamentally reshaped our comprehension of formal mathematical systems' limitations, while also provoking a surge in research exploring the diagonal lemma's ramifications across diverse fields of logic. Godel's original proof, however, relied on an arithmetized version of the lemma, introducing the concept of a Gödel numbering that assigned integers to syntactic expressions like formulas and sequences. By way of this finding, Hadamard's three circles theorem is extended to the setting of hyperbolic tubes in \mathbb{R}^{n}, specifically for n \geq 2, under the same differential equation condition.

Calibrating a camera's intrinsic parameters and estimating its extraneous pose are fundamental tasks in robotics. While traditional methods rely on manually placed markers or feature points, this study explores the use of a single rigid sphere for both purposes. The research relies on the geometric properties of the sphere's circular projection to solve the Perspective-n-Point (PnP) problem. By deriving the circular projection equation, the authors solve for the sphere's center and radius to complete intrinsic calibration. Subsequently, camera poses are determined by solving the PnP problem using the derived spherical model. The paper also presents a dedicated solution for the sphere-based absolute pose problem, which simultaneously handles pose estimation and synchronization. Finally, experiments validate the proposed methodology, demonstrating its efficacy.

Inverse problems involve reconstructing an unknown object from data corrupted by noise, a scenario prevalent in diverse fields such as imaging, signal and image processing, as well as medical diagnostics. Typically, these problems yield multiple solutions, among which only a limited subset aligns with observed data and incorporates prior knowledge. Consequently, generating a sample from the posterior distribution becomes a critical objective. This study introduces a novel variational inference algorithm specifically designed for ill-posed inverse problems. The proposed method integrates stochastic gradient descent with a newly defined "informed" momentum term. At each iteration, the algorithm updates an average model state and simultaneously refines a parallel auxiliary state. We demonstrate theoretically that the sequence of average models converges to within a controllable distance of the true posterior mean. Empirical evaluations across various test cases indicate that this approach outperforms existing methods in both computational speed and accuracy.

Invariant sets feature prominently in analyzing dynamical system behavior, with a specific focus on smooth invariant manifolds. This survey offers a comprehensive overview of existing literature on various types of invariant sets, including fixed points, periodic orbits, limit cycles, stable/unstable manifolds associated with these elements, as well as attractors, repellers, and the strange attractors central to chaos theory. Additionally, it examines the identification and characterization of these structures within both discrete-time maps and continuous flows.

The burgeoning demand for high data rates and network capacity has driven the adoption of terahertz (THz) communications, despite introducing significant path loss challenges. To mitigate these issues, this study proposes a THz-enabled cellular architecture integrating reflective intelligent surfaces (RIS) to enhance line-of-sight links. The primary objective is to maximize sum rates by optimizing a coupled system comprising THz beamforming at reflective intelligent surfaces (RIS) and base stations (BS). To address the non-convex nature of the problem, we introduce an efficient iterative algorithm combining successive convex approximation (SCA) and weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) techniques. Furthermore, the work addresses a secondary rate maximization problem under minimum power constraints using a similar SCA-based approach. Simulation outcomes validate the efficacy of the proposed method, demonstrating substantial improvements in spectral efficiency and overall system performance relative to benchmark solutions.

Scattering screens within the interstellar medium are investigated by analyzing radio scintillation data from pulsars. This study examines the influence of source size and the deconvolution process on the determination of screen properties, utilizing a Gaussian profile to represent the screen. Analysis of deconvolved scintillation curves is performed to estimate the screen's half-width ($w_{\rm{screen}}$) and the effective source radius ($\theta_S$). Utilizing pulsar data from the ATNF pulsar catalog, we calculate $\theta_S$ values and apply them alongside deconvolved curves to assess scattering curve characteristics. Our findings indicate that screens associated with distant pulsars are typically smaller than the standard 10 $\mu$as assumption, whereas screens for nearby pulsars are generally too small to be reliably measured. We further demonstrate that the screen's half-width is significantly overestimated if the source is assumed to be point-like when its source size is comparable to or exceeds $10 \, \mu$as. Conversely, for sources smaller than $10 \, \mu$as, the impact of source size on the measurement is negligible.

This study introduces a pitch-dependent dilated convolutional neural network designed to learn pitch-specific mappings in pitch conversion tasks. By integrating these models into a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) framework, the research achieves robust and high-fidelity generation of audio waveforms for pitch alteration. Experiments indicate that these proposed models outperform standard convolutional neural network-based approaches in both subjective evaluations and objective metrics.

This study presents the GiDiMo project, which involves the creation of a collection of annotated German morphological data. The primary objective is to develop a tool capable of accurately determining the lemma and morphological tags for English sentences based on their lemmata and tags. We examine a quantum point contact formed by two gapped graphene antidot resonators positioned in series, where the system is governed by an interdot interaction strength $U$. At low temperatures, a Majorana peak emerges in the tunnel conductance when $U$ surpasses the intradot energy level spacing $\delta$. This peak exhibits linear dependence on both temperature and bias voltage. Furthermore, the conductance scales inversely with the square root of bias voltage at elevated temperatures. By analyzing the finite-size scaling of the Majorana peak, we determine that the associated Majorana mode is spatially confined within a single antidot.

The swift advancement of deep learning has propelled intelligent detection algorithms to new levels of maturity, finding extensive application in road surveillance for identifying cracks, potholes, and other surface anomalies. Nevertheless, current studies often overlook the critical need for a comprehensive crack dataset, instead relying on merging existing defect databases that are inadequate due to low crack volumes and poor balance. Furthermore, these studies frequently employ a baseline convolutional neural network (CNN) network architecture, failing to assess the potential improvements offered by state-of-the-art models. To address these gaps, this research introduces the CrackDet dataset, assembled from over 10,000 crack images harvested from web sources. Leveraging this robust dataset, we developed RoadCrackDet, an adaptation of the COICODet framework tailored for crack detection. Experiments conducted on this new dataset demonstrate that RoadCrackDet achieves an mIoU score of 79.6% and outperforms other leading methods by a margin of 4.6%.

Grounded in the observation that pre-trained video-language models (VLMs) often inherit the localization deficiencies of their visual backbones, we introduce **LocAlign**, a training strategy designed to enhance sound source localization (SSL) within sound-annotation-rich video datasets. Our approach operates in two stages: the first involves mining hard negative samples from existing data to refine localization capabilities, while the second refines global alignment using self-supervision. Specifically, we identify alignment errors in language generation by comparing the actual visual content against the predicted transcripts. By selecting the top-k most relevant frames as positive samples and the remaining frames as negative samples, we compute a contrastive loss to optimize the alignment of generated text with accurate visual grounding. Experimental results confirm that LocAlign significantly boosts localization accuracy across multiple public benchmarks compared to state-of-the-art methods.

Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have emerged as a leading deep learning framework for tasks involving graphs, including classification and prediction. However, their effectiveness relies heavily on the graph's geometric properties, particularly when graphs possess scale-free or hierarchical structures, which can be best captured by hyperbolic geometry. While recent research has explored the utility of hyperbolic spaces for data representation, the application of hyperbolic geometry to graph learning remains an emerging field. This paper introduces Hyperbolic Graph Convolutional Networks (HGCN), a novel architecture designed to learn directly in hyperbolic space. By defining graph convolution operations within the Poincaré ball model of hyperbolic geometry, HGCN enables efficient processing of tasks such as link prediction and node classification. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets confirm that HGCN achieves state-of-the-art performance in link prediction and node classification. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that learning graphs directly in hyperbolic space yields superior results compared to approaches that learn embeddings in Euclidean space and subsequently map them to hyperbolic structures.

This work addresses the inversion of a structural acoustic partial differential equation model, where a sound source inside a fluid domain generates vibrations on an adjacent elastic structure. Beginning with a clear formulation of the associated PDE and source term, the authors present two novel methods for identifying an unknown excitation source from observational data. These approaches involve either a direct minimization of a cost function or a gradient-based scheme utilizing an adjoint state. Convergence theorems for both strategies are established, and numerical simulations are provided to validate the proposed techniques.

This study presents a method for exchanging and transporting squeezed states across two independent optomechanical setups linked by a three-level atom. Specifically, the exchange of squeezed vacuum states occurs between optical modes of the first setup and the carried squeezed state resides within the mechanical mode of the second system after the atom passes through. Our analysis reveals that this process achieves a high degree of fidelity even in scenarios involving mixed initial states. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of this approach as an effective means of long-distance squeezed state transfer within optomechanical architectures.

This paper introduces an extension of modal $\mu$-calculus incorporating set-variable predicate constants, a choice generalized from first-order logic. We demonstrate that, despite this added expressivity, decision for the underlying model-checking task remains feasible within specific frameworks. Furthermore, a novel characterization is offered, linking the equivalence problem for certain structured formulas also decided within limited ranges. In addition, formula translation functions are developed, allowing equivalent forms in pure modal $\mu$-calculus to be generated for formulas describing reached states within targeted models. Finally, distinct syntactic classes are identified within this expanded expression language; for formulas derived from these classes, it is shown that equivalent expressions in pure modal $\beta$-logics can likewise be generated.

We introduce a new methodology for estimating individual-level delay discounting and impulsivity by utilizing within-subject variation in choices across different contexts. Our approach addresses the constraints of traditional techniques, which often demand extensive data from repeated trials on identical options—a requirement that is frequently unmet in practice. Instead, our framework analyzes data from single-pass experiments featuring diverse stimulus sets. We demonstrate the practical application of this method using data from the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth 1997 (NLSY97), revealing substantial heterogeneity in delay discounting and impulsivity that existing methods failed to detect. Furthermore, we show that these individual estimates facilitate more precise statistical inference regarding the effects of delay discounting on economic behaviors.

The concept of negative absolute temperature, first proposed over a century ago, has long remained theoretical due to the inability to replicate conditions where high-energy states are more populated than low ones. Recently, this limitation was removed through an experiment at Aalto University, demonstrating negative temperature in an atomic system. A temperature below the absolute zero mark signifies that statistical mechanics and thermodynamics are deeply interconnected, challenging the conventional view that they are separate disciplines.

However, this breakthrough raises new questions regarding the precise requirements needed to generate negative temperature and the specific behaviors these states exhibit. Addressing these issues, a new study by a group led by Valtteri Havas explores the phenomenon using mean-field theory and Monte Carlo simulations. Their findings reveal that both isolated and interacting systems can achieve negative temperature, yet they display distinct characteristics.

In an isolated setting, the study finds that as a system transitions from positive to negative temperature, it undergoes a phase transition marked by a sudden jump in entropy—a counterintuitive outcome that defies standard expectations. Conversely, systems that interact with a heat bath approach negative temperature gradually, a process accompanied by entropic heating rather than a sharp transition. These results offer valuable insights into the underlying physics of negative temperature and its diverse manifestations across different thermodynamic environments.

Let $G$ denote a finite subset of an additive abelian group, and for any $A \subseteq G$ and coefficients $\alpha \in \{0, 1\}$, define the **restricted signed sumset** as:
$$
\widehat{\alpha} A = \left\{ \sum_{a \in S} \alpha a \mid S \subseteq A, \alpha a \in \{a, -a\} \right\}.
$$
Assuming $1 \le |A| \le |G| - 1$, and for any $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $k$-power of the set be denoted as $\widehat{\alpha} A^k = k \cdot \widehat{\alpha} A$. In this paper, we establish new lower bounds for the cardinality of the set $\widehat{\alpha} A^k$ when $k \ge 2$. Specifically, for $k=2$, these results improve upon those previously obtained by Hamidoune and Li. Furthermore, we identify conditions under which these proposed bounds are sharp.

Characterizing colorectal polyps via histopathological analysis is essential for assessing cancer risk and guiding appropriate management. Although deep learning has significantly advanced medical image analysis, the scarcity of annotated datasets has hindered its widespread application. To address this, we introduce a comprehensive public dataset comprising 1,000 whole-slide images (WSIs) of colorectal polyps, gathered from 855 patients treated between 2009 and 2019 at the University of Michigan. These images were annotated by three experienced pathologists, who labeled both tissue regions and corresponding diagnoses. We developed a disease-semantic-aware convolutional neural network (CSA-Net) to facilitate rapid annotation and deliver high-quality results. Our experiments on this dataset demonstrate that our model achieves a F1 score of 0.849 for region annotation and 0.885 for diagnosis. Furthermore, we introduced a user study showing that pathologists find our annotation system useful, efficient, and accurate. Collectively, these datasets, models, and annotation tools offer a vital resource for advancing colorectal polyp research through deep learning.

Pyroxenes from the H chondrite parent bodies serve as critical reservoirs for understanding the early history of water on these asteroids. This study reports new pyroxene and whole-rock analyses of the Benenitra and Chelyabinsk H chondrites, both of which experienced thermal metamorphism and subsequent impact melt events. The samples exhibit hydrogen isotopic ratios ($D_{\text{pyroxene}} = 180$ to $310\permil$, $\delta D_{\text{whole rock}} = 190$ to $310\permil$) that align with previously established ranges for H chondrites. Furthermore, the data indicate that the hydrogen inventory in these meteorites was largely established early in their history, before the onset of thermal metamorphism.

Using the algebraic Bethe-ansatz method, we construct the exact form-factor expansion applicable to the periodic XXZ spin chain, which exhibits $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetry. We demonstrate that the transfer-matrix eigenvalue and associated normalized local operators derived within this expansion are strictly invariant under the chain's symmetry, which is defined by the affine $SU(2)$ algebra. This finding holds true regardless of the specific arrangement of spins and supercharges along the chain. Our findings indicate that the complete set of form factors for local operators is determined by a few fundamental building blocks.

Speech Translation (ST) involves converting spoken language in one source to written form in another, utilizing Neural Machine Translation (NMT) as the core methodology. A critical research avenue in ST is zero-shot translation, where a model generates translations between pairs of languages it has not explicitly learned. Achieving this requires the model to understand the relationships among languages it encounters during training but does not hear translation pairs for. Current approaches achieve this by leveraging cross-lingual semantic embeddings to capture these relations. However, these methods face a challenge: they need vast amounts of parallel data for every language pair present in a multi-language system to ensure high-quality representations, which is often unavailable. Furthermore, existing models typically treat all languages and pairs equally, ignoring the inherent diversity among languages and the significant variation between specific translation combinations. This study introduces a new framework for zero-shot ST that utilizes contrastive learning to represent semantics. Our framework explicitly accounts for multi-language system dynamics by incorporating two key factors: (1) the diversity among languages and (2) the variation in performance across different source-target pairs. Extensive experiments on the Multi30k dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

This work evaluates three methodologies for calculating electromagnetic multipoles: Cartesian, spherical harmonic, and Gaussian fit. We conclude that Cartesian multipoles yield the optimal Gaussian beam waist and displacement, whereas a Gaussian fit produces the most accurate description of the beam's shape.

This study extends the theory of double Schur elements, initially defined by the author in 2019, to encompass Schur elements associated with the Kronecker (tensor product) representations of $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ and $\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}$. For these cases, these extended elements are expressed as sums involving Schur indices indexed by a novel combinatorial structure called double Young-Capelli bitableaux. These bitableaux were further utilized to derive a commutation formula for Schur indices of Kronecker $\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}$-Schur indices and $U_q(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$ Schur indices.

We examine the internal coherence of simplicity and phenomenological features within the simplest scoto-seesaw model, a two-Higgs-doublet model extended with two heavy sterile neutrinos and two light scalar singlets. In this framework, the "atmospheric" mass scale arises as a ratio of the heavy neutrino masses, while the "solar" scale is determined by the matrix product of the relevant Yukawa coupling matrices. We demonstrate that these scales are interdependent, constrained by the necessity of generating the correct atmospheric neutrino mixing angle. Additionally, we analyze the parameter space to determine the minimum values for the solar scale and the required ratio between the solar and atmospheric scales.

We present a straightforward model for calculating $d$-orbital branching ratios, addressing scenarios where hybridization occurs between $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ states due to significant mixing of the crystal field splitting parameter ($\Delta$) with crystal field splitting ($Dq$). We demonstrate the applicability of this model by analyzing branching ratios in vanadium and nickel oxides using X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) data. Our findings indicate that assuming purely $t_{2g}$-like final states can yield misleading conclusions when unoccupied $d$-orbital states contain substantial $e_g$ character, a factor that can also influence the outcomes of photoemission studies.

This study establishes a mirror-theoretic proof of the birational degeneration principle for relative quantum cohomology over toric complete intersection intersection varieties. By applying this result to specific degeneration scenarios, we derive the well-known geometric method of birational degeneration for quantum cup products in the toric variety $\mathbb{P}^n$.

Utilizing generative adversarial networks (GANs) for image-to-image translation has become a significant research focus in recent years. Our study demonstrates the capability of StyleGAN to produce highly realistic synthetic chest X-rays, an achievement that required approximately three weeks of training on 100,000 real images drawn from the CheXpert dataset. We evaluate the utility of these realistic samples in generating robust medical image analysis models, specifically concentrating on chest pathology detection using deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Our findings indicate that models trained on real and mixed synthetic datasets achieve performance comparable to those trained solely on real data. Furthermore, we observe that synthetic images alone yield competitive results on the CheXpert test set for three specific disease classifications: pleural effusion, pneumothorax, and atelectasis. Finally, we investigate potential performance disparities between models trained with synthetic data and those trained exclusively on real data, known as domain shift, and we explore strategies to mitigate this effect.

This paper presents a novel approach to modeling and analyzing high-dimensional vectorial data, which are characterized by both magnitude and directional attributes across many dimensions. To achieve this, we employ a recently developed directional regression framework that integrates the multivariate skew-elliptical distribution for data magnitudes with a multivariate copula for directional components. We introduce Bayesian methods for parameter estimation and posterior inference, and to facilitate posterior sampling, propose an efficient algorithm combining Gibbs sampling with importance sampling. An illustrative analysis of the global stock market dataset is conducted, and a comprehensive simulation study is performed to validate the proposed methodology.

This paper presents an algorithm for evaluating Newtonian potentials through a surface integral formulation. The method relies on approximating the surface with a set of flat panels and utilizes Green's third identity to derive the surface integral. For the standard $1/r$ kernel, the resulting panel integrals are solved exactly, whereas for other kernels, they are computed numerically to any desired precision. Consequently, the algorithm produces results that are more precise than those achieved by standard panel methods, which approximate the density as constant across each panel.
